accordion.name: accordion
accordion.use: Collapsible sections of related content such as FAQs or settings groups. Built on native <details>; use tabs when users compare sections, and a plain card when everything should be visible.
accordion.states: open attribute on a details item
accordion.notes: Zero JavaScript: <details> toggles, and giving every item the same name="..." makes the group exclusive (opening one closes the others; supported by current browsers, older ones simply allow several open). The summary holds the heading text and a chevron icon that rotates when open; the content is any block markup after the summary. Add open to expand an item by default. The summary is the control: keep its text short and put long content inside. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem each summary is at least 44px high. Spacing (0.27.0, proposal 129): the content block after the summary has one density step of padding on every side, so a form control or a switch row does not touch the summary; only direct p, ul and ol children are set in muted small text, components inside keep their own colour and size.
a11y: Native <details>/<summary>: Tab reaches the summary, Enter or Space toggles it, and browsers announce expanded/collapsed with no ARIA.
The chevron is decorative (aria-hidden); the open state is also in the DOM (open attribute), not only the icon.
Keep summary text meaningful on its own; do not put interactive elements inside the summary.
The focus ring is drawn inside the summary so it is not clipped by the rounded container.
The rotation of the chevron is shortened to nearly instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Use one shared name for an FAQ so only one answer is open.
Keep summaries to one line.
Open the most important item by default.
dont: Do not hide content users need to complete a task.
Do not nest accordions.
Do not put buttons or links inside the summary.

alert.name: alert
alert.use: Inline message about the page or a form, or (with alert--banner) a page-level message across the content width. Not for transient confirmations (use toast) or blocking decisions (use a dialog).
alert.markup: FailedCould not save.
alert.notes: Two markups. Classic: .alert > strong.alert__title + text. Rich: .alert > span.alert__icon.icon.icon--NAME + .alert__body (title + text) + optional .alert__actions (buttons, or a dismiss icon button). Use the icon for the tone: success circle-check, info info, warning triangle-alert, error circle-alert. Use role="alert" only for messages that appear after a user action or an error; role="status" for polite updates; no role for static page content. Placement: add alert--banner for a message that speaks for the whole page (maintenance, degraded service, expiring trial, read-only mode): it spans the content width, keeps only the top and bottom border and has no radius. Put it at the top of .main, above .content. Same icon, body, actions and tones as an inline alert. A button with data-banner-dismiss inside it hides it (toast.js) and emits design:close; remember the dismissal yourself if it should stay gone after a reload. It replaces the deprecated banner component.
a11y: Status is never colour only: the title says it and the icon shape matches the tone (decorative icons are aria-hidden).
role="alert" interrupts screen readers; use it for errors that appear after an action. Use role="status" for polite updates and no role for static messages.
A dismiss button is an icon-only button with an aria-label naming what it dismisses.
Actions are ordinary buttons or links in DOM order after the message.
Contrast: text on each tone background meets 4.5:1 in both themes and all accents.
A page banner present at load is ordinary content in reading order (first in main or just under the header); insert one later with role="status" (role="alert" for errors) so it is announced.
do: Lead with a short title, then one sentence of detail.
Offer the next step as an action when there is one.
Place the alert next to what it is about.
Use alert--banner for one page-level message at a time; combine messages.
dont: Do not stack many alerts; merge or prioritise.
Do not use role="alert" for static content.
Do not rely on tone colour alone.
Do not stack several alert--banner messages.

avatar.name: avatar
avatar.use: A person, team or account: photo, initials or a fallback icon. Not for logos or file icons.
avatar.notes: Size follows density (default is the control height; sm is the small control height); avatar--lg (0.21.0, proposal 078) is a fixed 4rem disc for the identity block of a profile header and ignores density. Put the change-photo and remove buttons next to a large avatar as ordinary buttons, never as a hover-only overlay. Named avatar: role="img" with aria-label (or inside). Decorative avatar next to the visible name: aria-hidden="true". Status: put a .dot inside the avatar and include the status in the accessible name ("Ada Lovelace, online").
a11y: A named avatar is role="img" with an aria-label (or an with alt text). A decorative one next to the visible name is aria-hidden="true" so the name is not read twice.
Initials alone are not a name: provide the full name in the label.
The status dot is decoration; fold the status into the accessible name and show it as text where it matters.
Groups use role="group" with a label, and the "+N" avatar says how many are hidden (aria-label="3 more people").
Avatars are not interactive; wrap one in a button or link yourself if it should be, which gets the standard focus ring.
do: Use two letters for initials.
Keep one size per list or table.
Give the group a label.
dont: Do not use an avatar for a logo or file type.
Do not use colour alone for presence.
Do not overlap more than about five avatars.

badge.name: badge
badge.use: Short status or label text, tag, or filter chip. For a status that needs more words use alert.
badge.states: aria-pressed on a <button class="badge"> filter chip; disabled
badge.notes: Status badges carry an icon and text, e.g. Running; colour alone is never the signal. Removable: a badge__remove
a11y: A badge is plain text; a screen reader reads it in place. Do not rely on colour: pair status tones with an icon and a word.
Decorative icons use aria-hidden="true".
A removable badge's button is named for what it removes (aria-label="Remove tag design"); focus returns to a sensible element after removal (your code).
A clickable badge is a real <button> or <a>, so it is keyboard operable with the standard focus ring; toggles expose aria-pressed.
Contrast: each tone's text meets 4.5:1 on its background in both themes and all accents.
On touch devices (coarse pointer or phone width) the remove button's hit area grows to 44px wide without changing the chip.
do: Keep text to one or two words.
Use the tone that matches the meaning (error = failure).
Use aria-pressed for filter chips.
dont: Do not use a badge as a button without making it a <button>.
Do not use colour as the only signal.
Do not put long sentences in a badge.

breadcrumb.name: breadcrumb
breadcrumb.use: Shows where the current page sits in a hierarchy and gives a way back up. Put it in the top bar or above the page header; not a substitute for the main navigation.
breadcrumb.states: aria-current="page" on the last item; aria-expanded on breadcrumb__more; hidden on collapsed levels
breadcrumb.markup:
1. Home
  2. Projects
  3. Bridge A12
breadcrumb.notes:
Structure:
>
    >
  1. . The separators are drawn by CSS, so they are not read aloud and need no markup. The last item is the current page: a (or a link with aria-current). The list wraps on narrow screens and long labels break. To collapse a long trail, keep the first and last two levels visible, add
    3. after the first, and put the hidden levels in
  3. . js/behaviors/breadcrumb.js reveals them on click and moves focus to the first revealed link (no menu is needed). Without the behaviour (or in React, which keeps its own state) toggle the hidden attribute and aria-expanded yourself. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem each breadcrumb link is at least 44px high.
a11y: A <nav> landmark with aria-label="Breadcrumb" containing an ordered list; screen readers announce the list length and position.
The current page carries aria-current="page".
Separators are CSS-generated content with no text, so they are never read aloud.
The collapse button exposes aria-expanded and a label that states how many levels it hides; activating it moves focus to the first revealed link.
Icon-only items (home) need an aria-label.
do: Start at the root and end at the current page.
Collapse only the middle of a long trail; keep the first and last levels.
Keep each label as short as the page title allows.
dont: Do not use it as the only navigation.
Do not show it on top-level pages (a one-item trail adds nothing).
Do not put text separators such as "/" or ">" in the markup.

button.name: button
button.use: Any action: submit, save, open, delete. One .btn--primary per view at most. For navigation to another page use a link; use <a class="btn"> only when the link must look like a button.
button.states: disabled attribute, aria-disabled=true (for links), aria-busy=true (action running), aria-pressed=true (toggle button)
button.notes: Icon-only buttons need an aria-label. Links styled as buttons use <a class="btn">. Busy: set aria-busy="true", put a .spinner first and keep the label; aria-busy does not block clicks, so ignore them in your handler (or add aria-disabled). Labels wrap instead of overflowing, so long translations stay inside the button. Inside .btn-group the buttons share borders and the focused or hovered one is drawn on top, so exactly one focus ring is complete at a time. A split action is a .btn-group with the main button and the arrow button (popovertarget + aria-haspopup="menu"), followed by a popover .menu; a filled (primary or danger) split shares one fill across both halves with a divider between them. Danger is a solid fill (--error with --on-error text).
a11y: A native <button> is focusable and activates with Enter and Space; a link styled as a button (<a class="btn">) activates with Enter only, which is correct for navigation.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label (or aria-labelledby) that names the action, not the picture; the icon itself is aria-hidden.
aria-pressed turns a button into a toggle: the name stays the same and the state is announced as pressed or not pressed.
aria-busy marks work in progress, it does not stop clicks: guard the handler. Keep the label so the name does not change under the user.
Disabled buttons leave the tab order. If a user needs to know why, give a visible explanation next to it instead of a tooltip on the disabled button.
The focus ring is the base outline; in a btn-group the focused button is drawn on top so the ring is never half hidden. Controls are at least 24 by 24 px (the control tokens).
do: Use one primary button per view and put it where the eye ends (right end of a form actions bar).
Name the action with a verb: Save, Export, Delete project.
Use a danger button only for destructive actions and confirm them.
dont: Do not use a button for navigation to another page: use a link.
Do not use a disabled primary button as the only way to explain a missing field: show the error.
Do not use an icon-only button without an aria-label.

card.name: card
card.use: The standard container for a group of content. Add card--interactive when the whole card leads somewhere. Do not nest cards. Add card--compact for dense grids and card--headed so the header reads as a filled band.

density: compact (tighter padding, inline footer, no divider)
header: headed (filled header with a hairline below)

card.notes:
Header, body, footer are all optional. Collapsible card:
Title
...
. card--interactive uses the stretched-link pattern: exactly one inside .card__title covers the whole card (its ::after), so the card has one tab stop and one accessible name; buttons in .card__actions or .card__footer stay separately clickable above it. Never wrap the whole card in an that contains buttons or other links. card--compact: header and body padding is space-3, the title is base size, and card__footer sits inline under the content without a divider. card--headed: the header is filled with the muted surface and a hairline, the end side holds card__actions (for example a badge); the body keeps its top padding. Both combine with each other and with card--interactive. Collapsible card with actions (0.19.0, proposal 041): the React CollapsibleCard builds card > card__header (a ghost btn--sm toggle holding a chevron icon and .card__title, then an optional status, then .card__actions at the end) + card__body stack (an always-visible slot such as a progress bar, then the collapsible region with id and hidden). The toggle sets aria-expanded and aria-controls; the chevron points right when closed and down when open. Only the toggle opens the body; buttons in card__actions never do. Use
when the header holds no buttons. The examples below show the markup in its closed and open state; the state change itself comes from CollapsibleCard (or your own code that flips aria-expanded, hidden and the icon). In a compact collapsible card the title inside the toggle is small and semibold (font-size-sm), like a tab label.
a11y: A card is a plain container: give it a heading (card__title as h2/h3 matching the page outline) or aria-label so it is easy to find; use <article> for self-contained items and <section> for groups.
card--interactive has a single link inside the title. The card gets one tab stop and the link text is its accessible name; do not duplicate it with an aria-label.
Controls inside an interactive card (card__actions, card__footer) are raised above the stretched link and keep their own focus and names.
Focus on the stretched link draws a visible ring around the whole card; in forced-colors mode it uses Highlight.
Collapsible cards use native <details>: Enter/Space toggle, state is announced, no script.

Collapsible card (CollapsibleCard): the toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the region, so Enter and Space open and close it and it is one tab stop; the chevron is decorative and changes with the state. Buttons in the header actions are separate tab stops and never toggle the card. Pass headingLevel to wrap the toggle in a heading for the outline.
do: Use one heading per card.
Keep header actions to two or three buttons.
Use card--interactive for navigation to a detail page, with the link in the title.
Use card--headed card--compact for grids of small, self-contained items such as add-ins.
dont: Do not nest cards or put a card inside a table cell.
Do not make a card clickable by adding a click handler to a div.
Do not put several links in an interactive card's title area.
Do not put more than a badge or one or two small buttons in the card__actions of a headed card.

carousel.name: carousel
carousel.use: A row of cards that scrolls sideways one position at a time, with arrows, dots, a counter and optional autoplay (discovery tiles, feature highlights). It hides cards that are off screen, so use it only when the content is optional or reachable elsewhere; use a grid when everything must be seen.
carousel.states: aria-current="true" on the active dot; aria-disabled="true" on prev/next at an end (not with data-loop); data-playing on .carousel while autoplay runs; data-fits when every slide is visible (controls and dots hide); aria-pressed on the pause button

carousel.notes: The track (.carousel__track, tabindex=0) is a native scroll-snap strip: swipe, wheel, trackpad and the arrow keys scroll it with no script, and Tab into a link inside an off-screen slide scrolls it into view. The behaviour (plain pages) or <Carousel> (React) adds the controls. Each slide is a .carousel__slide group named "n of N" (aria-roledescription="slide") holding a card. The next card peeks in so it is clear there is more. Controls come first in tab order, then the track, then the dots, one dot per slide: positions the strip cannot reach (when two slides share the last view) hide their dots, and the counter counts positions. Labels are page text: translate the aria-labels, data-template ("{current} of {total}") and the pause button's data-label-resume. Autoplay is opt-in (data-autoplay in milliseconds). It never runs under prefers-reduced-motion, stops while the pointer is over the carousel, while focus is inside, while the tab is hidden or the carousel is off screen, and stops for good after the first manual action until the pause button is pressed again. The pause button is required whenever autoplay is on (WCAG 2.2.2). The active dot fills over the delay while it runs. Dispatches design:change {index, slide}. A carousel is a size container: place it in a block-level parent. A slide change (arrows, dots, autoplay) is animated by the behaviour itself over --carousel-duration (default var(--duration-slider), 500ms; set it on .carousel in ms or s), eased in and out, because the browser's own smooth scroll cannot be given a duration. Scroll-snap is off only while the animation runs, and a finger, wheel or key press during it takes over. Under prefers-reduced-motion the strip jumps.
a11y: A section named with aria-label and aria-roledescription="carousel"; each slide is a group named "n of N" with aria-roledescription="slide" (W3C APG carousel pattern).

The track is focusable and scrolls with the arrow keys; the previous, next and dot buttons are ordinary buttons and the active dot has aria-current="true". At an end the arrow gets aria-disabled and keeps focus.

Autoplay is opt-in and always comes with a pause button first in the tab order; it stops on hover, focus inside, a hidden tab, an off-screen carousel, prefers-reduced-motion and after any manual action (WCAG 2.2.2).
aria-live on the track is "off" while rotating and "polite" otherwise, so manual changes are announced and automatic ones are not.
Position is never colour alone: the counter says "2 of 4" and the active dot is wider as well as accent coloured. Dots are 28px targets.
In forced-colours mode the dots use ButtonText and the active one Highlight; scroll-behavior is instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Keep slides to the same height of content and the same structure.
Give every slide a name that makes sense as a dot label ("Go to Excel add-in").
Use autoplay only for optional content, and keep the delay at 6 seconds or more.
Translate every label, including the counter template and the resume label.
dont: Do not put content the user must see (warnings, required steps, prices) only in a later slide.
Do not turn autoplay on without the pause button.
Do not nest carousels or put a carousel inside a scrolling track.
Do not use it for page navigation or a stepper; use tabs, steps or pagination.

chart.name: chart
chart.use: Styling for SVG charts, hand-built or drawn with d3: axes, grid, lines, areas, bars, points, legend, tooltip and empty state, with colours from the chart-* tokens. Not a charting library: you supply the geometry.
chart.states: Series colour is an attribute, never a class: data-series="1".."8", data-step="1".."6", data-diverge="-3".."3", data-muted. Lines add data-dash="1|2|3". Focusable marks (tabindex=0) get the normal focus ring.
chart.notes: Put class="chart" on the <svg> (and on a wrapping <figure> when you want a caption, legend or tooltip). Use a viewBox close to the size it renders at (about 640 by 320): text is in SVG units, so it scales with the drawing. Categorical colours chart-1..chart-8 are ordered so the first few are the most distinct; use at most 8 series, and fewer is better. They are checked for colour-vision deficiency (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) but still pair them with dashes, direct labels or legend shapes. The sequential ramp (chart-seq-1..6) and the diverging ramp (chart-div-neg-3 .. chart-div-pos-3) change lightness monotonically. Chart colours are independent of the accent. Using with d3: append elements with the class names above, set data-series from the series index, and call axes on groups classed chart__axis (d3 draws path, line and text children, which are styled). Draw a grid by calling an axis with a negative tickSize and an empty tickFormat on a group classed chart__grid. In forced-colors mode lines use CanvasText and marks use Highlight, so keep the dash patterns and direct labels.
a11y: Give every chart role="img" on the <svg> with <title> and <desc> (aria-labelledby), or an aria-label, and say what it shows including the headline finding.

Provide the data as text: a visually hidden table (<div class="sr-only"><table>...) next to the SVG, or a visible <details> with a table. The SVG is an image to assistive technology, the table is the content.
Wrap the chart in <figure> with a <figcaption> that states the metric, unit and period.
Never rely on colour alone: add dash patterns (data-dash), direct labels at line ends, legend swatch shapes (data-shape) and, for heatmaps, a ramp legend plus the data table.
Series and ramp colours are at least 3:1 against surface and surface-raised; axis and label text is at least 4.5:1 (checked by the build).
Tooltips are a convenience only (pointer and focus); everything they show must also be in the data table. Interactive marks need tabindex="0" and an aria-label with the value.
In forced-colors mode lines draw in CanvasText and bars in Highlight; direct labels and dashes carry the distinction.
do: Start bar charts at zero.
Label lines directly at their end and keep the legend short.
Use at most 5 series; mute context series with data-muted.
Use the sequential ramp for magnitude and the diverging ramp only around a meaningful midpoint.
dont: Do not pick colours yourself or use the accent for a series.
Do not encode meaning in colour only.
Do not use 3D, dual axes or truncated bar axes.
Do not put essential values only in a tooltip.

choice.name: choice
choice.use: Checkboxes and radio buttons with a label, hint and error, singly or in a group with a legend. Card style for options with a title and description (plans, shipping). For an immediate on/off setting use switch.
choice.states: checked, :indeterminate (set with data-indeterminate or the indeterminate property), disabled, aria-invalid=true on the input
choice.notes: The input stays a native checkbox or radio (class choice__input, appearance removed); only the box is drawn. Label it with for/id, not by wrapping, so the hint can sit under the label. Group related choices in <fieldset class="choice-group"> with a <legend class="choice-group__legend">; radios share a name. Group errors use field__error and aria-describedby on the fieldset. data-indeterminate on a checkbox sets the indeterminate state; data-check-all="#container" makes it a select-all parent (input-extras behaviour).
a11y: They are native checkboxes and radios: Space toggles a checkbox, arrow keys move within a radio group (one tab stop for the group), and form, validity and autofill behaviour are unchanged.
Name each input with a visible <label for>. Name a group with <fieldset> and <legend>; screen readers read the legend before each option.
Hints and errors are linked with aria-describedby; mark invalid inputs with aria-invalid="true" and show the message as text.
The checked state is drawn as a mark inside the box (check, dash or dot), never by colour alone; card choices also change border width in forced-colors mode.
The indeterminate state is visual only: it is not a third value, the checked value is still submitted as before.
do: Phrase checkbox labels so that checked means yes.
Use a fieldset and legend for every group of two or more.
Pre-select the safe default for a radio group when there is one.
dont: Do not use a checkbox for an immediate on/off setting: use switch.
Do not use radios for a yes/no question: use a single checkbox or switch.
Do not put interactive content (links) inside a card choice.

code-block.name: code-block
code-block.use: A framed block of source code, commands or config with a language label, a copy button, optional line numbers and highlighted lines. Use inline <code> for a word or two; use log for streaming output.

length: code-block--clamped: long blocks show 15 lines with a fade and a code-block__more button under the body

code-block.states: data-highlight on a .code-block__line marks it. data-token on any inner span styles it (keyword, string, number, comment, function, variable, type, punctuation). The copy button sets data-copied for 2 seconds. code-block--clamped: data-clamped on the block shows the clamped body; removing it opens the block, and the height animates on the motion tokens (none under reduced motion).
code-block.markup:
TypeScript
import { useState } from "react";

// Doubles a number; clamps negative input to zero.
export function double(value: number): number {
  return value < 0 ? 0 : value * 2;
}
code-block.notes: Markup: .code-block > .code-block__header (.code-block__lang + .code-block__actions > button[data-copy]) + pre.code-block__body[tabindex=0] > code > one span.code-block__line per line. Each line span ENDS with a newline character inside the span and there is no whitespace between line spans; this keeps selection and copy exact. The body scrolls horizontally and is focusable (tabindex=0) so keyboard users can scroll it. The copy button (copy.js) copies the block's text, or the element named by data-copy-target="#id"; it announces "Copied" in a polite live region, and falls back to execCommand and finally to selecting the text when the Clipboard API is unavailable (for example on plain http). There is NO syntax highlighter: a highlighter should emit <span data-token="keyword|string|number|comment|function|variable|type|punctuation"> and the block colours those with status and text tokens (all 4.5:1). Map your highlighter's scopes to these eight names (for example highlight.js hljs-keyword to keyword, hljs-title.function_ to function, hljs-built_in to type). React: <CodeBlock code="..." language="TypeScript" numbered wrap highlight={[3]} renderLine={...} /> (wrap adds code-block--wrap). code-block--wrap wraps long lines (pre-wrap, anywhere) instead of scrolling sideways; use it for a View options > Wrap text toggle by adding or removing the class. Line numbers stay on the first row of each line.
a11y: The code body is a scrollable region and has tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys.
The copy button is a real <button> with an aria-label (or visible text); activating it announces "Copied" through a polite live region, so the result is not only an icon change.
Highlight, number and token colours never carry meaning alone: highlighted lines also get a bar, and comments are italic. Text colours are 4.5:1 or better against the block.
Line numbers come from CSS and are neither selectable nor part of the copied text.
In forced-colors mode token colours are dropped (text keeps its system colour) and highlighted lines keep an accent bar.
do: Always label the language; it also tells screen reader users what they are reading.
Keep one command per block when people will paste it.
Put the exact text people should copy in the block; show prompts like $ only in prose.
dont: Do not insert whitespace or newlines between line spans.
Do not use it for long streaming output (use log).
Do not paste a third-party theme: map the highlighter to data-token.

combobox.name: combobox
combobox.use: Choosing one or several values from a long list by typing to filter it (country, assignee, tags from a set). Short lists (up to about seven options): use a select or choices. Free text that is not limited to a list: use tag-input.
combobox.states: aria-expanded on the input; data-active on the highlighted option; aria-selected on options; aria-busy on the list while loading; .combobox__empty[data-loading]; disabled and aria-invalid on the input
combobox.markup:
Germany
Austria
combobox.notes: ARIA 1.2 editable combobox with list autocomplete. Markup: .combobox (add data-combobox to switch the behaviour on) > input.combobox__input[role=combobox] + .combobox__list[role=listbox] > .combobox__option[role=option] (optionally inside .combobox__group[role=group][aria-label][data-label]). The list needs a name: aria-labelledby the field label or aria-label. Give options data-value (default: their text). aria-selected=true in the markup preselects. data-name="country" keeps hidden inputs in step so a native form submit works. Multiple: data-multiple plus a chips host (.combobox__chips right after .combobox, or data-chips="#id"): chosen values become badge chips with a remove button and the list stays open. Async: data-async; the behaviour fires design:query {query} (debounced, data-debounce ms) and shows a loading message; answer with el.designCombobox.setOptions([{value,label,group,disabled}]) or setLoading(false). Events: design:select {value, values, label}. Results are announced in a polite status region ("5 results available", "No results"); translate with data-text-results, data-text-none, data-text-loading, data-text-selected, data-text-removed, data-text-remove. Filtering ignores case and accents. Focus never leaves the input; the highlighted option is named by aria-activedescendant. React: <Combobox>. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem each option is at least 44px high. The chip remove buttons (.badge__remove) stay small, see proposal 062. Chip remove buttons keep their size but get a 44px-wide hit area on touch devices (from badge).
a11y: Pattern: WAI-ARIA APG editable combobox with list autocomplete. The input has role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls (the listbox), aria-autocomplete=list and aria-activedescendant for the highlighted option; keyboard focus never leaves the input.

Keys: Arrow Down opens the list and moves to the next option (to the chosen one first), Arrow Up moves to the previous or opens at the last, Home/End jump to the first/last option while one is highlighted, Enter chooses the highlighted option, Escape closes the list (a second Escape clears the text), Tab closes it (and chooses a highlighted option in a single select). Typing filters the options (case and accent insensitive).
The number of matches ("5 results available" or "No results") and each choice or removal is announced through a polite role=status region, so users who do not see the list know what happened.
Selected options carry a check mark and aria-selected (and are not told apart by colour alone); disabled options have aria-disabled and are skipped by the arrows.
Multiple: the listbox is aria-multiselectable and stays open; each chosen value is a chip with a remove button named "Remove <label>"; removing returns focus to the input.
Async: while loading, aria-busy is set on the list and a visible Loading message is shown; announce failures yourself.
do: Give the list an accessible name and the input a visible label.
Show enough options at once to be useful and keep the list scrollable.
Use the async mode for server-side search and debounce it (data-debounce).
dont: Do not use it for fewer than about seven options: a select is simpler.
Do not allow values that are not in the list unless you handle them: use tag-input for free text.
Do not put interactive content inside an option.

command.name: command
command.use: A command palette: one keyboard-first search box that jumps to pages and runs actions (Ctrl/Cmd+K). Use it as a shortcut layer on top of normal navigation and menus, never as the only way to reach something.
command.states: aria-selected="true" on the active option; aria-disabled="true" on an unavailable item; hidden on filtered-out items, groups and the empty message; data-command-hotkey on the dialog enables Ctrl/Cmd+K
command.markup:
SettingsCtrl,
No matching commands
command.notes: Built on the same native <dialog> as the modal (js/behaviors/dialog.js opens it with [data-dialog-open="id"] and handles Escape and backdrop click). js/behaviors/command.js adds the combobox/listbox model: the input keeps focus and aria-activedescendant points at the active option; typing filters by label and data-keywords (case- and accent-insensitive, every word must match); empty groups update, and while nothing matches the listbox is hidden and the .command__empty message (a sibling of the list) shows; the number of results is announced through a polite status region. Enter (or a click) runs the active item: an <a href> is followed, and every run emits design:select on the dialog with detail { value, item } (value = data-value or the label) before the dialog closes. Add data-command-hotkey to open and close it with Ctrl/Cmd+K from anywhere. The first match is active again after every keystroke. React: CommandPalette.
a11y: The input is a combobox (role=combobox, aria-controls, aria-expanded, aria-autocomplete=list) over a role=listbox of role=option items; DOM focus never leaves the input, aria-activedescendant names the active option and aria-selected marks it.

Keys: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move (wrapping), Page Up/Down jump to the first/last result, Enter runs the active item, Escape closes the dialog and returns focus to where it was. Ctrl/Cmd+K toggles it when data-command-hotkey is set.
Each filter change announces "N results" (or the empty message) through a polite role=status region.
The dialog needs a name (aria-label or aria-labelledby) and the input an accessible label; groups are role=group, their .command__heading is presentational and referenced with aria-labelledby.
Selection is never colour alone: the active option has a thick start border as well as a tint, and in forced-colors mode it uses the system highlight colours.
Everything in the palette must also be reachable without it: it is a shortcut layer.
do: Give every item a verb or destination label and an icon; add data-keywords for synonyms.
Show the keyboard shortcut of an action in .command__shortcut.
dont: Do not put forms, long lists or destructive actions that need confirmation straight in the palette; open a modal for those.
Do not hide the only route to a page behind the palette.

diagram.name: diagram
diagram.use: Focus state for the parts of a generated SVG diagram (a Mermaid flowchart, a section or plan drawing): the renderer marks one node and its links as lit and everything else as dim. Not a diagram renderer and not for HTML controls.

focus: diagram-part--dim: out of focus, faded to --opacity-dim (0.25)

diagram.states: Set by the renderer, not by the system. While a node is in focus the renderer puts diagram-part--lit on that node and its links and diagram-part--dim on every other part; with no focus no part has either class. data-focus on the svg is the renderer's own hook (the design system does not read it). The change animates on --duration-fast and --ease (none under reduced motion).
diagram.markup: <svg class="chart" viewBox="0 0 240 80" role="img" aria-label="Two steps, the first in focus"><g class="diagram-part diagram-part--interactive diagram-part--lit"><rect x="8" y="20" width="80" height="40" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/></g><path class="diagram-part diagram-part--lit" d="M88 40H152" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/><g class="diagram-part diagram-part--interactive diagram-part--dim"><rect x="152" y="20" width="80" height="40" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"/></g></svg>
diagram.notes: The renderer adds the classes to the elements it generated (for Mermaid: g.node and path.flowchart-link) and removes them to clear the focus. Add diagram-part to every part that can change, diagram-part--interactive to the ones that react to the pointer, and toggle --lit and --dim. The outline is a ring of 1px drop-shadows in the accent colour on the part's shapes (rect, circle, ellipse, polygon, path), not a stroke: generators set stroke and fill with ID selectors that outrank every class, and the system does not use !important. Text inside a node is never outlined. On a thin link the outline reads as a slightly thicker accent line with the original line in the middle. In forced-colors mode the outline uses Highlight and nothing is faded. A part that can be lit must also be reachable without the pointer: the renderer is responsible for keyboard access (tabindex and key handling) and for a text alternative of the diagram.
a11y: The focus state is a visual aid only: the lit outline (accent against the surface) and the fade do not carry meaning that is missing elsewhere. Give the diagram a text alternative that lists the nodes and their links.
Dimmed parts stay at 25% opacity and are not meant to be read while dimmed; the renderer clears the focus on a second click, on Escape or when the pointer leaves, so no content stays hidden.
A part that reacts to the pointer must also react to the keyboard (tabindex="0", Enter or Space toggles the focus); the base focus ring applies to focusable SVG elements.
The transition is switched off under prefers-reduced-motion. In forced-colors mode the outline is drawn in Highlight and nothing is faded.
do: Light the selected node and its links together, so the connection is visible.
Clear the focus with a second click or Escape.
dont: Do not use dim to hide content the user still needs to read.
Do not set stroke or fill on a diagram part to show focus; the system uses the outline.
Do not use these classes on HTML controls.

divider.name: divider
divider.use: A thin line that separates sections or inline items, optionally with a centered label ("or"). Prefer spacing; use a divider when the grouping needs to be visible.
divider.notes: Use <hr class="divider"> for a real thematic break (it is a separator for assistive technology). For a purely visual line use <div class="divider" role="separator">. Vertical: <hr class="divider divider--vertical" aria-orientation="vertical"> between inline items in a .cluster or toolbar. Dividers have no margin: space them with stack/cluster gaps.
a11y: <hr> maps to role=separator, so it is announced as a separator between sections. Do not add an extra role.
A divider made from a div needs role="separator"; add aria-orientation="vertical" for vertical ones. If it is purely decorative use no role and aria-hidden="true".
A label inside a separator is presentational for some assistive technology; keep the meaning in the surrounding content (the buttons say what they do).
The line meets 3:1 against the surface only as a hint, never as the sole carrier of meaning; in forced-colors mode it uses CanvasText.
do: Use spacing first, a divider when grouping must be seen.
Keep the label to one or two words.
dont: Do not use many dividers in a row.
Do not use a divider as an empty spacer.
Do not put essential content only in the label.

dot.name: dot
dot.use: A small status marker next to text (online, failing, draft). Never use it alone: the status must also be said in words.
dot.notes: A dot is decoration: mark it aria-hidden="true" and put the status in text beside it ("Online", "3 failing"). Colour alone is never enough (colour-blind users, forced-colors mode, screen readers). For a stronger status use badge with an icon. Inside an avatar the dot sits in the corner (see avatar).
a11y: The dot is aria-hidden and conveys nothing by itself; the adjacent text is the status.
Colour is reinforcement only: success, warning, error and info are distinguishable by the words, and forced-colors mode shows every dot in CanvasText.
The dot has no interactive behaviour and is not a tab stop.
Do not put the dot's only meaning in a title or tooltip.
do: Write the status next to it.
Use the same tone for the same meaning everywhere.
dont: Do not use a dot alone to show status.
Do not animate it to attract attention.
Do not use it as a bullet for ordinary lists.

drawer.name: drawer
drawer.use: A side sheet for details, filters or a longer form that should keep the page visible behind it. Use a modal for a short decision, a popover for a small panel, and the shell sidebar for navigation.
drawer.states: open attribute on the dialog; data-dialog-static disables backdrop light dismiss
drawer.markup:
Session details

...
drawer.notes: Built on the same native <dialog> as the modal, so the browser provides the focus trap, Escape, the inert page and focus return, and js/behaviors/dialog.js provides [data-dialog-open] / [data-dialog-close], backdrop light dismiss and design:open / design:close (shared code, nothing to add). It slides in from the end edge (the start edge with drawer--start, mirrored in right-to-left); below 40rem it fills the width. Header and footer stay put, only .drawer__body scrolls. The slide is removed with prefers-reduced-motion. A dialog that is open without showModal() renders in the page flow as a static preview. React: Drawer. Width: add drawer--wide for a document or image preview opened from a list (72rem, still full width below 40rem); React: <Drawer size="wide">.
a11y: A drawer is a modal dialog: it needs an accessible name (aria-labelledby on the heading in .drawer__header); behaviours warn in the console when it is missing.
showModal() moves focus into the drawer, keeps Tab inside, makes the page inert and returns focus to the trigger when it closes.
Escape closes it, and so does a click on the backdrop unless data-dialog-static is set. Always include a visible close button.
The slide animation is removed with prefers-reduced-motion; the sheet works the same in right-to-left layouts (the start/end sides mirror).
A scrolling body that has no focusable content needs tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.
do: Keep the page behind it meaningful: use a drawer when users still need to see context.
Put primary and secondary actions in the footer so they never scroll away.
Use drawer--wide for a document or image preview opened from a list.
dont: Do not open a drawer from another drawer or modal.
Do not use it for site navigation; the shell sidebar already becomes a drawer on phones.

dropzone.name: dropzone
dropzone.use: Adding files by dropping them or by choosing them from the file dialog, with a list of what was chosen. For a single attachment in a form the plain file input in field is enough.
dropzone.states: data-target (the zone appeared because a drag is in progress elsewhere; data-target="danger" for a destructive target such as a recycle bin), data-dragover (a file is over it),aria-invalid=true (rejected files), aria-busy=true (uploading), aria-disabled / disabled; file-list__item[data-state=busy|done|error]
dropzone.markup: PDF or images, up to 5 MB each.
dropzone.notes:
A real is stretched invisibly over the whole area (class dropzone__input), so clicking, Enter and Space open the native dialog and dropping a file works even without script. Add data-dropzone to .dropzone for the behaviour (dropzone behaviour; React: ): it highlights while dragging (data-dragover), checks files against accept, data-max-size (bytes) and data-max-files, lists accepted files in the .file-list named by data-list (or the next sibling), keeps input.files in step so a normal form submit works, and gives each file a remove button. Rejected files set aria-invalid on the dropzone and the input and fire design:invalid {files:[{name, reason: type|size|count}]}; show the message yourself in a .field__error linked with aria-describedby. Accepted files fire design:files {files}. Uploading is yours: call el.designDropzone.setBusy(true) and setStatus(file, {text, state, value}) (value 0 to 100 draws a progress bar). Put the constraints in the hint so they are read with the name. Translate announcements with data-text-added, data-text-removed, data-text-rejected, data-text-remove. DROP TARGET (data-target): for a zone that is only shown while something is dragged (chats onto a recycle bin, files from another window), set data-target on .dropzone when the drag starts and remove it (or the zone) when it ends. It gets an accent border, slides up and fades in over the base duration, pulses its border colour slowly while idle, and on data-dragover fills in, takes the stronger border colour and scales its icon slightly. data-target="danger" does the same in the error colours. All motion is off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (the coloured border and fill remain). data-target is only a look: the app owns the drag events and the drop; keep the same action reachable without dragging. Such a zone usually has no file input, so it is plain markup:
Drop to delete
.
a11y: The file input is the control: it is focusable, its name is the label text, Enter and Space open the file dialog, and a screen reader announces it like any file input. The hint with the constraints is linked with aria-describedby.
Drag and drop is an extra, never the only way: everything works from the keyboard through the native dialog.
Adding, removing and rejecting files are announced in a polite role=status region; a rejection also sets aria-invalid, and the page shows the reason as text.
Every file has a remove button named "Remove <file name>"; after removing, focus moves to the next remove button or back to the file input.
Progress bars are native <progress> with the file name as their label and the status is also written as text, so progress is not colour or graphic alone.
The dragover state changes border style (dashed to solid) as well as colour; the focus ring surrounds the whole area.

A data-target zone is a visual cue only; its motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion, and in forced-colours mode the border is drawn in the Highlight colour. The icon and label text say what the drop does, so it is not conveyed by colour alone.
do: State accepted types and the size limit in the hint.
Show per-file status as text as well as a bar.
dont: Do not make drag and drop the only way to add files.
Do not hide the real file input with display none: that removes it from the keyboard.

empty.name: empty
empty.use: Nothing to show yet: first use, no results, an empty list or a failed load. One action at most. For a transient message use alert or toast.
empty.markup:
No sessions yet

Scan this PC to find your sessions.
empty.notes: Say what is missing, why, and what to do next. Icons use the icon classes (never glyphs). Put an empty state inside a card or a table cell with empty--compact.
a11y: The icon is decorative (aria-hidden); the title and text carry the meaning.
Use a real heading level for the title when the empty state is a main part of the page; the default is a styled div for use inside tables and cards.
For an empty state that appears after a user action (search, filter), announce it with a polite live region (role="status" on the results region).
The action is a normal button or link with a clear label.
Error tone is not colour only: the icon shape, the title and the text say it failed.
do: Explain what to do next with one clear action.
Use empty--compact inside cards and tables.
dont: Do not show an empty state while data is still loading (use loading).
Do not use more than one primary action.
Do not use emoji or glyphs instead of icon classes.

error-summary.name: error-summary
error-summary.use: A block above a form that lists every problem found on submit, each as a link to its field, and takes focus when it appears. It does not replace the message under each field.
error-summary.states: hidden until there is a problem; the behaviour focuses it when it is shown
error-summary.markup:
There are 2 problems

  • Email: enter an email address
  • Terms: accept the terms
error-summary.notes: A <section> named by its heading (aria-labelledby) with tabindex="-1" so it can take focus. It deliberately has no role="alert": the error-summary behaviour moves focus to it, which announces the heading once; an alert would announce the same text again on top of that. (If you show a summary without moving focus, add role="alert" to it yourself.) Each list item is a link to a field's id; the behaviour focuses the field on click (a bare #fragment does not reliably focus form controls) and for a group (fieldset) its first control. The behaviour focuses the summary whenever it goes from hidden to visible. el.designErrorSummary.show([{id, message}]) renders the list, shows and focuses it. For plain HTML forms add data-error-summary to the summary and put it inside a <form novalidate>: on submit it lists every invalid control (label plus the browser's message, or a data-error attribute on the control), sets aria-invalid, creates a .field__error linked with aria-describedby when the field has none, and removes an error as soon as its field is valid. Write link texts as "Field: what is wrong", the same words as the message next to the field. Translate the heading with data-text-title and data-text-title-many ("{n}").
a11y: The summary is a named region (aria-labelledby the heading) and takes focus when it appears, so a screen reader announces the heading ("There are 2 problems") once and the user can move through the links; sighted keyboard users see the focus ring on it.
It has no role=alert. An alert is announced when it is inserted, and focusing it announces it again, so using both double-announces. Use role=alert only when you show a summary without moving focus.
Links move focus to the invalid field (a plain #fragment link does not reliably focus form controls). Radio groups and fieldsets focus their first control.
Fields keep aria-invalid="true" and a field__error linked by aria-describedby, so the problem is also read when the field is reached by any other route.
Colour is not the only cue: the heading carries an icon and the words, and the left border is thick.
do: Write link texts as the field name plus the problem: "Email: enter an email address".
Show the summary at the top and bring it into view.
Keep the order the same as the fields on the page.
dont: Do not add role=alert and also move focus.
Do not list problems that have no field to fix.
Do not replace the message next to each field with the summary.

field.name: field
field.use: Text inputs, selects and text areas with their label, hint and error. Wrap label + control + hint/error in .field. Checkboxes, radios and switches use choice and switch; combined controls use input-group, search, combobox and the others.

control: input (text, email, number, date, time, month, week, datetime-local, file)
hint: field__hint--ai: the AI fills the field in when it is left empty

field.states: disabled, readonly, required (use the attribute on the control plus data-required on the label), aria-invalid=true
field.markup: Shown in the list.
field.notes: Required: put required (or aria-required) on the control and data-required on the label; the asterisk is generated with empty alternative text, so screen readers hear "required" from the control exactly once. Optional text: data-optional="optional" on the label prints (optional) in any language you write in the attribute. Hint and error: give each an id and list them in aria-describedby on the control; set aria-invalid="true" while there is an error. The textarea grows with its content where the browser supports field-sizing and is capped. Native pickers (date, time, file) follow the theme. Control heights follow the density switch. Checkboxes, radios and ranges are plain elements. AI-filled field (proposal 102): a field is required, optional, or optional and filled in by the AI when left empty. Mark the last kind with data-optional on the label, a placeholder that says where the value comes from ("Read from the file"), and a hint with field__hint--ai whose first child is the sparkles icon; the page writes the text. Never mark a required field as AI-filled.
a11y: Every control needs a visible <label for>; placeholders are examples, never labels.
Required fields carry required (or aria-required) on the control. The asterisk on the label is decorative (empty alternative text), so it is not read a second time.
Hints and errors are separate elements linked with aria-describedby. Add aria-invalid="true" while a field has an error; remove both when it is fixed.
Errors are text, not just a red border. For a form with many fields also show an error-summary.
Read-only fields stay in the tab order and can be selected; disabled fields are skipped and not submitted.
Focus shows the accent border and the base focus ring; text and borders meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.
do: Put the hint under the label or the control, not in the placeholder.
Say what is wrong and how to fix it in the error.
Use the right input type (email, tel, number) so phones show the right keyboard and autofill works.
Tell the person what the AI does with an empty field, and show the result afterwards (for example a "read from the document" tag).
dont: Do not use the placeholder as the label.
Do not mark every field required: mark the optional ones when most are required.
Do not remove the focus outline.
Do not use the AI hint for a required field, and do not show it once the person has typed a value.

form.name: form
form.use: The layout of a whole form: vertical rhythm, titled sections, responsive rows of fields and a right-aligned action bar that can stick to the bottom of long forms. The controls themselves are field, choice, switch and friends.
form.markup: Account
form.notes: <form class="form"> stacks its children with the section gap and is a size container, so rows and the action bar react to the width of the form (a modal, a side panel, a phone) rather than the viewport. A section is a <fieldset class="form__section"> with a <legend class="form__legend">. .form__row puts fields side by side in as many columns of 14rem as fit and collapses to one column on its own. .form__actions is right-aligned with the primary action last; in a narrow form the buttons become full width and the primary action moves to the top. Pair with error-summary above the form; the form's own validation is native (add novalidate when you show your own messages).
a11y: Group related controls in a <fieldset> with a <legend> (form__section and form__legend): screen readers announce the legend with each control inside.
The reading and tab order is the DOM order; rows only change the visual layout, so keep related fields adjacent in the markup.
The primary action is last in the markup (and in tab order); in narrow forms it is shown first visually, which is a visual reorder only for the thumb, so keep the markup order as the logical one.
A sticky action bar stays inside the page flow (no focus trap) and leaves room for the phone home indicator through the safe-area inset.
Show validation as an error-summary on top plus a field__error under each field, all linked with aria-describedby / aria-invalid.
Everything wraps and reflows at 20rem; there are no fixed widths.
do: Split long forms into titled sections.
Put the primary action last on the right (first on a phone).
dont: Do not make two columns the only layout: rows collapse for a reason.
Do not hide required information in a placeholder.
Do not use a sticky bar in a short form that fits the screen.

guide-step.name: guide-step
guide-step.use: A numbered instruction in a setup or how-to guide: a number, a short title, and the content (text, a code box, a screenshot) indented under the title text. Use it for a list of things the reader does, one after the other. It shows no progress; for the state of a process (wizard, checkout) use steps.
guide-step.markup:
1. 1

    Open the Options dialog

    Run the command, then search for:
guide-step.states: None. The number is the list position (set a different first number with the start attribute on the ol).
guide-step.notes: An <ol class="guide-steps"> of <li class="guide-step">. Each item holds the number as <span class="badge badge--circle" aria-hidden="true">, the title as a heading element with .guide-step__title (choose the level that fits the page outline), and optional content in .guide-step__body. The ol already gives the position to screen readers, so the number badge is aria-hidden. A step with no content simply leaves out the body. Put key words in the title in <strong>. The body is a grid: its children stack with a small gap, align to the start and shrink inside it, so a code box or a screenshot in a body never stretches. The title is a plain block (inline emphasis keeps its spaces), 0.875rem medium and its first line is centred on the number; the body is 0.875rem regular, so the keywords in <strong> stand out. Screenshots are a figure in the body; cap their width with project layout CSS.
a11y: An ordered list: screen readers announce the position. The number badge is aria-hidden so it is not read twice.
The title is a real heading element chosen by the page, so the guide appears in the heading outline without skipped levels.
Emphasis in the title uses <strong>, so it is a weight difference as well as a colour-free signal.
Text uses the full text colour on every surface in both themes (4.5:1 or more); there is no state to signal by colour.
do: Keep each title to one action; put the detail in the body.
Put key words and commands in the title in <strong>.
Use the heading level that follows the page's headings.
dont: Do not use guide-step to show progress through a process: use steps.
Do not set sizes or indents in project CSS; the body is already aligned under the title.
Do not leave out the ol: it carries the numbering for assistive technology.

icon.name: icon
icon.use: Pictograms from the shared icon set (Lucide base plus our own). Never draw or paste an inline <svg> icon; if one is missing, add it to the set (see How to add one) or write a proposal.
icon.notes: Size: 1.25em, so an icon scales with the text around it; change the parent's font-size, never the icon's width. For a different size use icon--sm (1em, matches the text height) or icon--lg (1.5em); React: . Colour: currentColor, so an icon follows the text colour of its parent (muted text gives a muted icon; a disabled or ghost button dims its icon with it). Alignment: inline-block with a small downward offset so it sits on the text baseline; inside flex or grid containers (buttons, menu items, tabs) the gap is the component's job. Tone: icon--tone-success | -warning | -error | -accent colour a bare status icon with the matching text token (the same colours as badge--TONE text) when a boxed badge or a dot is too heavy, e.g. a notification or activity row. The shape still carries the meaning, so keep the word (visible or sr-only) next to it; under forced colors the tone is ignored. Do not use it for decoration. Labelling: icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden="true") because the text next to them carries the meaning. An icon-only button needs an aria-label on the BUTTON, not on the icon. A standalone icon that conveys meaning without text (a status marker) uses role="img" and an aria-label instead of aria-hidden. Never use an icon as the only cue for state; pair it with text or a title. Finding icons: search by concept with `node tools/design.mjs icons ` (for example `icons delete`, `icons chart`); every name is a class icon--NAME, a React Icon name (typed) and a sprite symbol. Use only listed names. How to add one: there is no ad-hoc icon. First look for it in Lucide (node_modules/lucide-static/icons/.svg): copy it unchanged to icons/lucide/.svg and add search keywords to a tags file (icons/tags..json, same shape as icons/tags.json: { "name": ["keyword", ...] }). If Lucide has none, draw our own: 24 by 24 viewBox, 2px stroke, round caps and joins, fill none, colours only currentColor, file icons/custom/.svg with keywords in icons/tags.json. The build validates the SVG and generates the class, the sprite symbol and the React name. Propose new icons through the proposal process if you are not maintaining the set. Forms: (needs icons.css; works on file:// pages) or (needs icons.svg and does not work on file:// pages). React: .
a11y: Decorative icons carry aria-hidden="true"; the adjacent text provides the name.
An icon-only button gets aria-label on the button; a standalone meaningful icon gets role="img" and an aria-label.
Icons inherit the text colour, so they meet the same contrast as the text; do not use an icon as the only indicator of state.
Icons scale with the font size and respect user text zoom; the click target belongs to the button, which is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
Tone never carries meaning alone: keep a word (visible or sr-only) beside a tone icon; the tone colours are the text tokens, so they meet 4.5:1 on the surface in both themes.
do: Use a listed name (node tools/design.mjs icons <concept>).
Let the parent set size and colour.
Add a missing icon to the set instead of inlining an SVG.
dont: Do not paste inline <svg> icons or use text glyphs (x, search symbols).
Do not set width, height or colour on the icon.
Do not use an icon without text or a label for anything important.
Do not tone an icon for decoration or to signal state without text.

input-group.name: input-group
input-group.use: An input with attached text or icon (prefix, suffix), a joined button (copy, search, apply) or a password reveal toggle.
input-group.states: disabled and aria-invalid=true on the input (the addon follows)
input-group.notes: Children: .input-group__addon (text or icon), .input and .btn in any order. They share borders; the focused one is drawn on top. The input still needs its own label (a <label for> in the surrounding .field, or aria-label). Addon text that matters is part of the label: say it in the label too, or link it with aria-describedby. Password reveal: a button with data-password-toggle and aria-controls=<input id> (input-extras behaviour): it switches the input between password and text and keeps focus on the button; with aria-pressed the label is constant, with data-label-pressed the label changes instead.
a11y: The input keeps its own label; a decorative prefix such as https:// is hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden) so the label is not cluttered. If the addon changes the meaning (EUR), link it with aria-describedby.
Icon addons are decorative. A joined button needs its own visible text or aria-label.

The password toggle is a real button with aria-controls. With aria-pressed the name stays "Show password" and the state is announced; with data-label-pressed the name changes and aria-pressed is removed, so the state is never announced twice. Focus stays on the button.
The visible text of a revealed password is not announced; the button label is the only feedback, so keep it honest.
The focused part is drawn above its neighbours so the focus border is complete.
do: Use an addon to show units or fixed text the user should not type.
Keep the label outside the group, as for any field.
dont: Do not put an interactive control inside an addon: use a .btn child.
Do not use an addon as the only label.

kbd.name: kbd
kbd.use: Key caps for keyboard shortcuts in help text, menus and documentation. Styles the <kbd> element directly; the .kbd class is for a span or for places where a component resets kbd.
kbd.notes: Write a combination as separate <kbd> elements joined by a plain "+" text (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>P</kbd>); the outer <kbd> around the whole combination is also valid but styles it as one key. Name keys in words (Esc, Enter, Tab, Ctrl) rather than glyphs, with the platform symbol in the text where it differs: on macOS write Cmd instead of Ctrl and Option instead of Alt. Show the shortcut for the user's platform when you can detect it; otherwise name both (Ctrl or Cmd). Keys that are only symbols (arrows) need a text alternative: <kbd aria-label="Left arrow">...</kbd> with an icon, or write Left.
a11y: <kbd> is read as ordinary text, so always spell keys as words (Ctrl, Shift, Enter); a screen reader reads each key and the plus signs.
Never rely on the key cap look to mean "clickable": a key cap is not interactive.
State the shortcut for the user's platform (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) and make every shortcut also reachable by a visible control.
Key cap text is 4.5:1 or better on its background; the cap keeps its border in forced-colors mode.
do: Use one <kbd> per key.
Use the same key names as the keyboard legends.
dont: Do not use <kbd> for text the user types (use <code>).
Do not use symbol-only keys without a text alternative.

kv.name: kv
kv.use: Key/value details (a description list): properties of one thing such as a server, an order or a user. For many items with several attributes each use table.

layout: inline (two-column grid: term column as wide as the longest term up to min(40%, 14rem), value column the rest; rows aligned; stacks below 16rem of container width)
cols (multi-column fact list, term over value, 14rem columns)

kv.notes: Native <dl>, <dt>, <dd> with the pairs as direct children (no wrapper divs). A term can have several kv__desc (each further value sits under the first). kv--inline is a two-column grid at any width: the term column fits the longest term (at most 40% of the container or 14rem, longer terms wrap), the value column takes the rest and wraps, rows align like a table, rows are 12px apart and the term sits 16px before its value. It needs no breakpoint: the kv is its own container and stacks term over value below 16rem of its own width, so it works in cards, sidebars and drawers alike. Because it is a size container (like form) it takes the width of its parent: put it in a block, a card or a growing grid/flex child. kv--cols lists many short facts in as many 14rem columns as fit (term over value, pairs never split, order runs down each column).
a11y: <dl>/<dt>/<dd> expose term-description relationships to screen readers; keep terms short and unique.
Do not put the dt and dd in separate containers; keep them adjacent children of the dl.
Values that are status use text or an icon with text, not colour alone.
Text wraps and long words break, so nothing is clipped at 20rem width.
do: Use short, noun-like terms.
Prefer kv--inline in cards and wide containers, kv--cols for six or more short facts, plain kv where terms are long.
Format dates and numbers consistently.
dont: Do not use kv for a form (use field).
Do not put block content such as tables in kv__desc.
Do not fix a pixel width on terms.

layout.name: layout
layout.use: Spacing, arrangement, responsive columns and page rhythm without writing CSS. Start with stack and cluster; reach for switcher, with-sidebar or grid--cols-N when a layout must adapt to the space it is given.
layout.markup:
Title

...
layout.notes: BREAKPOINTS. Three build-time values: sm 40rem (phone drawer, single column), md 56rem (icon rail), lg 72rem. CSS writes $bp-sm, $bp-md, $bp-lg inside @media or @container; media queries cannot read custom properties. Projects do not write breakpoints: use the helpers below, which already adapt. WHICH HELPER. Arrange children in one direction: stack (vertical), cluster (horizontal, wraps). Fill the width with equal cards whose count follows the space: grid (as many 18rem columns as fit) or grid--compact (12rem). Need exactly 2, 3 or 4 columns that drop to 2 and 1: grid--cols-N. Form beside an explanation: switcher (equal children) or with-sidebar (fixed-width aside, flexible main). Limit a reading width: center, center--narrow (28rem), center--prose (44rem). CONTAINER QUERIES. Wrap a region in .container and its descendants respond to the width of that region, not the screen: the same card grid fits a full page, a split pane and a dialog. grid--cols-N collapses with the nearest .container ancestor (4 and 3 columns become 2 below md, every count becomes 1 below sm); when there is no .container it falls back to the viewport width with the same steps. switcher and with-sidebar measure themselves and need no container. CONTAINER PITFALLS. .container applies inline-size containment: the element ignores its content when computing its width, so it must get a width from its parent (a block, a grid cell, a flex item with flex: 1). A shrink-to-fit flex item or inline element with .container collapses to zero width. An element cannot query itself: put grid--cols-N on a child of the container, not on the container. Do not put .container on .content. DENSITY. <html data-density="compact"> (theme.js: designTheme.setDensity("compact")) lowers --layout-control from 2.25rem to 2rem, --layout-control-sm from 1.75rem to 1.5rem, and --density-y/--density-x (row and cell padding) from space-3 to space-2. Use the density tokens for any padding that should follow. TOUCH (0.19.0, proposal 052): on a coarse pointer (touch) or below $bp-sm (40rem) both control tokens are raised to 2.75rem (44px), compact density included, so buttons, inputs, selects, Menu and Search triggers, segmented items, tabs and nav rows all reach the touch target size with no rule of your own; row and cell padding is not changed. Avatars and other things sized with the control tokens grow with them. Layout helpers keep their gaps: density is about controls and rows, not page structure. page-section gives marketing pages vertical rhythm from --fluid-section (2rem on a phone, up to 5rem). scroll-x lets a wide child scroll sideways inside its own box; give it tabindex="0", a role and a label so keyboard users can scroll it. hide-sm / show-sm helpers were deliberately NOT added: hidden content is a smell. Let components adapt (the shell collapses its sidebar by itself) or use a container query inside a component. NEW TOKENS (0.5.0): --layout-prose-wide 44rem (prose column), --layout-aside 18rem (with-sidebar aside), --fluid-section. FILL: fill goes on a child of a height-bounded flex column (a dock, a side pane, a .split__pane that is also a .stack) and makes it take the height that is left and scroll inside it (flex: 1 1 0; min-block-size: 0; overflow: auto). The usual use is the visible .tab-panel under a tab bar; a [hidden] panel stays hidden. fill does nothing in a parent that has no bounded height or is not a flex container.
layout.states: Layout helpers have no states. Density (data-density="compact" on <html>) shrinks control heights and cell padding for every component; it needs no class here. On a coarse pointer or below 40rem the control tokens are 2.75rem whatever the density.
a11y: Layout helpers are structure only: they never change reading or tab order. A visually reordered layout must keep a meaningful DOM order (with-sidebar puts the main content first in the DOM).
A scroll-x region must be keyboard reachable: tabindex="0", a role such as region and an aria-label; the base focus ring shows it.
Use sr-only for text that screen readers need and sighted users do not; never hide interactive elements with it.
Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10): switcher, with-sidebar and grid--cols-N reduce to one column at 20rem without horizontal scrolling.
A fill region that scrolls must be keyboard reachable: give a scrolling tab panel tabindex="0".
do: Use stack for vertical rhythm and cluster for rows of buttons or badges.
Wrap a split pane or a dialog body in .container so grid--cols-N follows its width.
Use switcher for a form beside help text and with-sidebar for content beside a fixed aside.
Put fill on the tab panel (or any one child) of a flex column with a bounded height, so only that child scrolls.
dont: Do not put .container on .content or on a shrink-to-fit flex item.
Do not write media queries in projects: the helpers adapt on their own.
Do not hide content on small screens to make a layout fit.

level-map.name: level-map
level-map.use: Shows a sequence of levels, such as the levels of a lab or course, with each level's state (passed, current or locked) and its stars, so a learner sees at a glance where they are. It wraps to rows on a narrow screen and never hides a level. For a process that runs once from start to end, use steps.
level-map.states: data-state="locked" | "open" | "current" on .level-map__node; aria-current="step" on the current node. "open" is an unlocked level that is not the current one; a passed level also shows the check icon in its marker, and that marker fills.
level-map.markup:
1. Level 1: Cost of exploring (passed)3 of 3 stars
  2. 2Level 2: Imagination pays (current)1 of 3 stars
  3. Level 3: Learning-rate noise (locked)Locked
level-map.notes: An <ol class="level-map" aria-label="..."> of <li class="level-map__node"> (or <li><a class="level-map__node" href="..."> when a learner can open the level from there). Each node holds .level-map__marker (aria-hidden: the position number, the check icon for a passed level or the lock icon for a locked one), .level-map__label (the level name, with a visually hidden state such as (passed), (current) or (locked)) and .level-map__stars (text such as "2 of 3 stars" or "Locked"). A star icon, if the page uses one, sits inside .level-map__stars and takes the accent-text colour. The map is a wrapping row: nodes grow to share a row and move to the next row when the width runs out, so no level is hidden. Nodes are not clickable by default; a link node keeps the same states.
a11y: An ordered list with an accessible name; the current level is aria-current="step" and its label says (current).
Markers are aria-hidden (the number repeats the position, the icons repeat the state); the label carries the level name and its state in visually hidden text.
A locked level has a dashed marker and the word Locked, so the state is not shown by colour alone.
Stars are plain text ("2 of 3 stars"); a star icon inside the readout is decorative.
As a link node the level gets the normal focus ring; a node that is not a link is not focusable.
In forced-colours mode the current level gets a Highlight border and a passed marker is filled with Highlight and HighlightText.
do: Show every level in order, including the locked ones, so the learner sees the whole sequence.
Put the stars of each level in its own node.
Make the node a link only when the learner can open that level from there.
dont: Do not hide levels on a phone; the map wraps instead.
Do not use it for a process that runs once from start to end; use steps.
Do not use it as navigation between unrelated pages; use tabs or the navbar.

link.name: link
link.use: Variants of the text link. A bare <a> is already the accent-coloured default link; add .link only for the variants below (or to give a non-anchor element the same look).
link.notes: link--external appends the external-link icon after the text. Use target="_blank" only when opening a new tab really helps the reader (they lose their place otherwise); when you do, add rel="noopener noreferrer" and a visually hidden hint such as (opens in a new tab) so screen-reader users are warned. Links to another site that open in the same tab still get link--external, with rel="noopener" only if they carry target. Links in running text keep their underline; do not remove it. A button.link (a link-styled button, for example in a table cell) is at least --layout-control-sm high (28px, WCAG 2.5.8); inside running text (p, li, .prose) it keeps one text line, like a link. Compact density lowers the token on purpose. A button.link (proposal 155) is reset to look like a link: no background, border or padding, the surrounding font.
a11y: Links keep their underline, so they are distinguishable without colour (WCAG 1.4.1); the muted variant still meets 4.5:1 text contrast.
The external icon is decorative (a CSS pseudo-element, not announced); say "opens in a new tab" in text for screen readers.
Focus uses the system focus outline; in forced-colours mode the icon follows the link colour.
do: Use meaningful link text ("Download the report"), not "click here".
Add rel="noopener noreferrer" with target="_blank".
dont: Do not open new tabs by default.
Do not style links as buttons; use .btn for actions.
Do not remove the underline in running text.

list.name: list
list.use: A vertical list of records with a title, optional meta line and actions (people, files, recent items). One column of items; for several columns use table.

actions: overlay (fades the row text under them)
hover (revealed on row hover or focus; with overlay)

list.states: aria-current on the current row (links), aria-pressed on toggle buttons, aria-selected="true" on selected rows inside role="listbox"; data-removing="true" plays the shared exit animation on list rows, and data-list-item="true" opts composite rows into that state; list__actions--hover: shown on li:hover, li:focus-within (keyboard) or while a control inside has aria-expanded="true"; always shown on touch screens (hover: none)
list.markup: • AtlasUpdated today
list.notes: Dividers are built in. Padding follows density. Static rows: the <li> is the .list__item. Interactive rows: the <li> wraps an <a class="list__item" href> (or a <button class="list__item">), so the row is one focus stop with a hover and focus state. Leading content (avatar, icon) is a direct child before .list__main; row buttons go in .list__actions and must not be placed inside a link (put the link and the actions side by side in a wrapper li instead, or open details from the row). aria-selected only belongs on role="option"/"row" elements, so use it for a real listbox and aria-current for navigation lists. Hover actions (0.23.0, proposals 069 and 083, the same mechanism as table--row-actions): add list__actions--hover (with list__actions--overlay) to .list__actions to keep it transparent until the row is hovered or has focus inside. The buttons stay in the tab order (opacity only, never display or visibility), so the row stays one tab stop and Tab moves on to its actions, which appear as soon as focus is in the row. Touch screens, which cannot hover, always show them. Put the link/button row and the actions side by side inside the li (siblings), never nested.
a11y: A <ul> with <li> children is announced as a list with its item count; keep real list markup (do not use divs).
Interactive rows are real <a> or <button> elements: one tab stop per row, Enter (and Space for buttons) activates, standard focus ring inside the row.
Mark the current row with aria-current (page, true); aria-selected is only valid on role="option" (listbox) or grid rows.
Icon-only action buttons need an aria-label naming the row ("More actions for Ada Lovelace").
Current and selected rows are tinted; the state is also exposed through the attribute so it is not colour only (add a check icon where selection must be visible).
In forced-colors mode current and selected rows use Highlight.

Hover actions are only made transparent, so they stay focusable and named; focusing the row or any control inside it reveals them (:focus-within), and touch screens always show them. Never rely on hover alone for an action.
do: Keep titles to one line of meaning and meta to one short line.
Use the same row structure throughout a list.
Use list for navigation-like records and table for comparison.
Use list__actions--hover for dense lists with two or three row actions (mark read, delete).
dont: Do not nest interactive elements (a button inside a link).
Do not put more than two or three actions in a row.
Do not use aria-selected on plain links.
Do not hide actions with display or visibility in project CSS; use list__actions--hover so they stay reachable by keyboard.

loading.name: loading
loading.use: Waiting states: a spinner for an action in progress, skeletons for content that is loading. Use progress when you know how far along it is.

skeleton: text (one line of text height, up to 12em wide)
text-reveal: (default) text appears left to right once, 600 ms

loading.states: aria-busy="true" on the container or button that is loading
loading.notes: Size block skeletons with layout CSS (width, height) in the app layer. Inside a busy button use spinner--current with aria-hidden and keep the button text. Keep the real structure (header, labels) and skeleton only the data.
