a11y: A standalone spinner needs role="status" and an accessible label; inside a button that already has text it is aria-hidden.
Skeletons are decorative: mark the loading container aria-busy="true" and announce "Loading ..." once through a polite status region.
Animations stop under prefers-reduced-motion (shimmer and spin are shortened) and in forced-colors mode they are static.
Do not move focus when content finishes loading unless the user asked for it.
do: Skeleton roughly the shape of the final content.
Keep static labels and headings visible while loading.
Remove skeletons as soon as data arrives.
dont: Do not show a spinner longer than a few seconds without a message.
Do not use skeletons for errors or empty results.
Do not make skeletons focusable.

log.name: log
log.use: A scrolling viewer for build, server or job output: one line per entry with time, level and message, following the newest line. For a real terminal emulator (xterm.js) use the terminal-* and ansi-* tokens instead; for source code use code-block.
log.states: data-level="debug|info|warn|error" on each .log__line. data-paused on the .log pauses following. The Jump to latest button (.log__jump) is created by log.js and hidden while following.
log.markup:
09:14:01 info Build started (node 24.1, 8 workers)
09:14:01 debug Resolved 412 modules in 118 ms
09:14:03 info Compiling src/app/main.ts
09:14:04 warn Deprecated option "legacyBuild" is ignored
09:14:06 info Bundled 3 chunks (1.2 MB)
09:14:07 error Cannot find module "./missing" imported from src/app/routes.ts
09:14:07 info Build finished with 1 error and 1 warning
log.notes:
Markup: .log[role=log][aria-live=off][tabindex=0][aria-label] > .log__line[data-level] > time.log__time + span.log__level + span.log__message, with a space between the three spans so copied text reads naturally. Give the log a height from layout (it defaults to a 24rem maximum) and an id when it has controls.

Levels are shown by a text label (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR), colour, and for warn and error a bar and tint; colour is never the only cue.

Follow tail (log.js): while the log is scrolled to the bottom, new lines keep it there. When the user scrolls up, or the log is paused, it stops following and a Jump to latest button with a count of new lines appears. Smooth scrolling is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion. Controls: a button with data-log-action="pause|wrap|clear|latest" and aria-controls="<log id>"; pause and wrap are toggles that keep aria-pressed. Events: design:follow {following, paused}, design:log-clear. There is no virtual scrolling: keep the DOM under a few thousand lines (remove old lines yourself).

Why aria-live="off": a log that streams would flood a screen reader with every line. Expose milestones separately (for example a role="status" line that says "Build failed") and let users read the log by moving into it (it is focusable and scrollable).

Pause and resume pattern: a toggle button with data-log-action="pause" and aria-pressed. While paused, lines keep arriving but the view stays put; resuming (or Jump to latest) scrolls to the end.

Terminals: xterm.js and similar emulators take colours from tokens. Read them at runtime and re-read on the design:theme event: const css = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement); const get = name => css.getPropertyValue('--' + name).trim(); then build the theme from this mapping (xterm ITheme key to token):
background = terminal-bg
foreground = terminal-fg
cursor = terminal-cursor
cursorAccent = terminal-bg
selectionBackground = terminal-selection
black / brightBlack = ansi-black / ansi-bright-black
red / brightRed = ansi-red / ansi-bright-red
green / brightGreen = ansi-green / ansi-bright-green
yellow / brightYellow = ansi-yellow / ansi-bright-yellow
blue / brightBlue = ansi-blue / ansi-bright-blue
magenta / brightMagenta = ansi-magenta / ansi-bright-magenta
cyan / brightCyan = ansi-cyan / ansi-bright-cyan
white / brightWhite = ansi-white / ansi-bright-white
terminal-selection is the only colour with alpha (rgba). Every ansi colour except black and bright-black is at least 4.5:1 on terminal-bg, black and bright-black at least 3:1, terminal-fg at least 7:1; in the light theme white and bright-white are mid greys so they stay readable on the light background.
a11y: role="log" with aria-live="off": new lines are not announced (a stream would drown the screen reader). Announce milestones with a separate role="status" element.
The log is focusable (tabindex="0") with an aria-label, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow, Page and Home/End keys and screen reader users can read it line by line.
Level is conveyed by text (DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR), plus a bar and tint for warn and error; level colours meet 4.5:1.
Text selection and copy are unrestricted. Time, level and message are separated by spaces so the copied line reads naturally.
Jump to latest is a real button with a visible label and the count of new lines; pause and wrap are toggle buttons with aria-pressed.
Following and the jump scroll are instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Keep a fixed maximum number of lines.
Use data-level on every line, even debug.
Show timestamps in a consistent format.
dont: Do not set aria-live="polite" on a streaming log.
Do not colour message text to mean severity; use data-level.
Do not use it for interactive shells (use a terminal emulator with the terminal tokens).

menu.name: menu
menu.use: A list of actions opened from a button (row actions, overflow menus, sort and view options). .popover is the same panel for any other content, e.g. a filter panel or a small form. Use a select for choosing a value in a form, and tabs or navigation for moving between pages.
menu.states: aria-expanded on the trigger; aria-checked on checkable items; disabled or aria-disabled on an item; data-danger=true for destructive items; data-keep-open keeps the menu open after an item is chosen; data-icon="true" keeps an option icon visible and reserves a trailing .menu__check slot; aria-checked=true shows the checkmark
menu.notes: Plain HTML: the Popover API does the opening, light dismiss and Escape; the panel is placed with CSS anchor positioning (js/behaviors/popover.js places and flips it in browsers without it) and menu.js adds the arrow-key model, typeahead and checkable items. React: the Menu helper renders the older .anchor > .menu pattern (only while open) with the same keyboard model, and accepts icons, shortcuts, checked items, separators and headings. TEXT TRIGGER (menu bars: File, Edit, View, More views): in plain HTML use btn btn--ghost btn--sm as the trigger (no btn--icon); in React pass triggerText="File" (it becomes the button's accessible name, so label only names the menu). PORTAL (row actions in a scrolling table or any clipping parent): in plain HTML the popover form already renders in the top layer; in React pass portal, which shows the open menu as a manual popover placed against the trigger (it flips above when there is no room below, is limited to the viewport and scrolls inside), keeps it against the trigger when the page or a scroll container moves it or the window resizes, and closes it once the trigger scrolls out of sight; a scroll that does not move the trigger (a carousel, a streaming chat) leaves it open. Without portal nothing changes. Menus are content-sized by default. Inside .anchor the menu is absolutely positioned and can be clipped by an overflow:hidden parent; prefer the popover form there. Put an icon first in .menu__item and a .menu__shortcut last; a checkable item may carry an option icon; it stays visible, and all checked options reserve a trailing .menu__check slot so menu width stays constant. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem each menu item is at least 44px high. Link items: a menu that goes to a page uses <a class="menu__item" role="menuitem" href> instead of a button, so middle-click, Ctrl/Cmd+click and Open in new tab work; in React give the item an href (and, in a single-page app, onSelect to navigate with the router: a plain click then cancels the default navigation, a modified click stays a plain link). A disabled link carries aria-disabled and no href. Fixed width (proposal 158): add menu--fixed (React: fixedWidth) to a panel with long labels; it is 1.5 menu widths, at most the screen width, and the labels wrap.
a11y: The trigger is a button with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded (menu.js and popover.js keep it in step); give an icon-only trigger an aria-label.
Enter, Space and click open the menu; ArrowDown opens it on the first item, ArrowUp on the last. Focus moves to an item on open.
Inside the menu: ArrowUp/ArrowDown move and wrap, Home/End jump, a letter jumps to the next item that starts with it, Escape closes and returns focus to the button, Tab closes and moves on.

Items use role=menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio; aria-checked reports the state. Disabled items stay focus-skipped but visible. Separators use role=separator; group labels are role=presentation (or label a role=group).
A popover (.popover) holds ordinary content and is not a menu: it has no menu roles and does not trap focus; give it an aria-label.
Menus never carry essential information that is not reachable elsewhere; the same actions must exist for people who cannot open the menu.

A text trigger names itself: the visible text is the accessible name (React triggerText leaves the aria-label off), so voice-control users can say what they see. The menu itself is named by its aria-label.

React picker (value select): `picker` makes the trigger a form select box (class `select`, the same as a native select) that shows `triggerText`; items are radio items for one value (shown without a radio button: the chosen row is tinted with a check at its end) or checkbox items with keepOpen for several; headings group them, `searchable` adds a filter field at the top, `onOpen` fires on each open, and the last items can be an action such as Manage. Open or focused shows the accent border. Use it instead of a native select when the list needs groups, search or an action; a short plain list stays a native select.

React panel="picker": the picker panel (menu--picker, radio rows tinted with a check at the end) on any trigger, such as a compact icon button, so the same choice looks the same at every width; `picker` (select-box trigger) already implies it. triggerTitle sets a hover tooltip (title) on the trigger; an icon-only trigger still needs its accessible name (label gives it as aria-label).
React footer:`footer={{ label, icon, onSelect }}` pins one action (Manage models) at the bottom of the panel under a line, in the accent text colour; it stays in view while the options scroll.

React size: the trigger is the compact 24px button by default; size="md" gives the standard icon button (the same size as btn--icon next to it) with the 16px icon, for toolbars and footers that mix menus with other icon buttons.

React portal: the open menu is a manual popover in the top layer, so no scrolling ancestor clips it; Escape, Tab, arrow keys and outside click behave as without it. It follows its trigger on scroll or resize and closes when the trigger is out of sight; scrolling elsewhere does not close it.
do: Put the most common action first and destructive ones last, after a separator.
Use sentence-case verbs ("Rename", "Export as CSV").
Show the keyboard shortcut in .menu__shortcut when one exists.
In a table with scrolling or clipping wrappers, open row-action menus in the top layer (React portal; the popover form in HTML).
dont: Do not nest menus inside menus.
Do not use a menu for navigation between pages; use navigation or tabs.
Do not put form fields in a .menu; use .popover.

modal.name: modal
modal.use: A focused dialog that blocks the page until it is answered: confirmations, short forms, details that need a decision. Use a drawer for longer side-by-side work and a popover for small, non-blocking panels.

layout: manager (fixed height, section list beside the content)

modal.states: open attribute on the dialog; data-dialog-static disables backdrop light dismiss; returnValue tells which button closed a form dialog
modal.markup:
Discard changes?

You have unsaved edits.
modal.notes: Native <dialog> is the default: showModal() gives the focus trap, Escape, an inert page behind it and focus return. js/behaviors/dialog.js adds [data-dialog-open] / [data-dialog-close] triggers, backdrop light dismiss, design:open / design:close events and a console warning when the dialog has no accessible name. Put header, body and footer directly in the dialog (or inside one <form method="dialog">): only .modal__body scrolls, so the title and buttons stay visible. Below 40rem every size except .modal--sm fills the screen; .modal--sm stays a compact card. Destructive confirmations use .btn--danger for the confirm button and keep Cancel first. A dialog that is open without showModal() (a static preview) renders in the page flow. The React Modal/ConfirmDialog helpers keep using the .overlay wrapper. Manager dialog (0.21.0, proposal 077): add .modal--manager to a .modal--lg (or --xl) for a dialog with a section list beside its content, such as a model manager, a profile or a settings dialog. Put the header, then .tabs-layout.tabs-layout--responsive-flush (React: <Tabs orientation="vertical" responsiveFlush />) directly inside the dialog with no wrapper: each panel holds one .modal__body that scrolls and, when the section has actions, one .modal__footer that stays put. The height is fixed (85dvh) so switching sections never resizes the dialog; below 56rem the section list becomes a bar above the panel and below 40rem the dialog fills the screen. The title is plain text, with no icon tile. Set data-density="compact" on the .modal__body when the panel is dense (many rows or cards); density applies to any container, not only <html>. Group the content with .eyebrow headings above .card blocks and .setting rows; instant-apply sections need no footer, a section with one Save button puts it in the footer.
a11y: The dialog needs an accessible name: aria-labelledby pointing at .modal__title (behaviours warn in the console when it is missing); add aria-describedby for the message of a confirmation.
showModal() moves focus into the dialog, keeps Tab inside, makes the rest of the page inert and returns focus to the trigger on close; do not rebuild this with scripts.
Escape closes it; a click on the backdrop closes it too unless data-dialog-static is set. Always give a visible Cancel or Close button as well.
Icon-only close buttons need aria-label="Close".
A scrolling .modal__body that has no focusable content needs tabindex="0" and a role/name so keyboard users can scroll it.

The .overlay > .modal form (React helpers) uses role=dialog (or alertdialog for ConfirmDialog) with aria-modal="true" and the helpers trap focus and handle Escape for you. ConfirmDialog focuses its confirm button on open (initialFocus="cancel" for an action that cannot be undone).
A manager dialog keeps the vertical tab list's roles and arrow keys (react/Tabs); the dialog itself needs one accessible name, which is its .modal__title.
do: Name the action on the confirm button ("Delete sessions", not "OK").
Keep dialogs short; move long forms to a page or a drawer.
Use <form method="dialog"> so buttons close the dialog and report returnValue.
dont: Do not stack dialogs more than one deep.
Do not open a dialog on page load or without a user action.
Do not use a dialog for a message that does not need an answer; use a toast or an alert.

nav-section.name: nav-section
nav-section.use: A titled group of sidebar rows that is always open ("Access", "System"). Use it for every sidebar list that has group titles, so the heading inset and the space between groups are the same everywhere.
nav-section.states: none; the heading is static text, not a control
nav-section.markup:
Access
Users & Roles
System
Global Settings
nav-section.notes: The heading is an .eyebrow inside .nav-section__heading, inset like the .nav-item rows. Consecutive sections are separated by --space-2. In the icon rail (56rem down to 40rem) the heading is hidden and the rows stay a plain list; in the phone drawer it shows again. A group with no visible rows is not rendered, so no empty heading appears. Use the shell's nav-item--section (a button with aria-expanded) when the group has to collapse. Do not set title spacing in project CSS.
a11y: The sections are plain groups of links inside one <nav> with an aria-label; the heading is visible text, so it is read in order with the rows.
The heading is not a control: it has no role and takes no focus. If the group must collapse, use nav-item--section (see shell) instead.
In the icon rail each row keeps its accessible name (give icon-only rows an aria-label or visible text in .rail-hide).
do: Use it for every sidebar list that has group titles.
Leave out a section that has no visible rows.
Keep titles short: one or two words.
dont: Do not set heading spacing or insets in project CSS.
Do not use it for a group that collapses; use nav-item--section (see shell).
Do not make the heading a link or button.

navbar.name: navbar
navbar.use: The top navigation of a website: marketing pages, documentation, public sites. Apps use the shell (sidebar + topbar) instead; do not combine the two.

width: navbar--contained (content capped at --layout-modal-xl and centred, for sites whose page content is capped the same way)

navbar.states: aria-current="page" on the current .navbar__link; aria-expanded on .navbar__toggle (phone panel open or closed)
navbar.markup:
Brand
Home
Get started
navbar.notes: A <header class="navbar"> placed directly in <body> is the page's banner landmark. Order inside: .navbar__brand, .navbar__toggle (the phone menu button), nav.navbar__links with .navbar__link anchors (aria-label="Main"), .navbar__actions for the theme toggle, a language switch and one call to action (btn btn--primary). The bar lines up with .content. On wide screens everything is inline. Below 40rem the toggle appears and the links and actions form a panel under the bar that the toggle opens: write aria-expanded="false" on the toggle and aria-controls pointing at the links' id; js/behaviors/navbar.js flips aria-expanded, closes the panel on Escape (focus returns to the toggle), on a link click and when the window grows. In React set aria-expanded from your own state: the CSS reads that attribute. .navbar--sticky pins the bar to the top; the page also gets a scroll-padding so anchor targets and focused elements are not hidden behind it. Put the .skip-link before the navbar and end the page with .site-footer. The theme slot takes the React ThemeToggle menu (Light, Dark, System); plain pages can use a mode select with Light, Dark and System options, or a button to toggle light/dark. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem the brand link is at least 44px high. .navbar--contained (0.30.1, proposal 214) caps the inner content at --layout-modal-xl and centres it while the background and border stay full width: use it with a page whose content is capped at the same width (e.g. a wrapper with max-inline-size: var(--layout-modal-xl)).
a11y: Banner landmark (<header> in <body>) with a labelled <nav>; the current page is aria-current="page" with a visible tint and underline, not colour alone (an outline in forced-colours mode).
On phones the toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls and a text alternative (aria-label="Menu"); the closed panel is display:none, so it is out of the tab order.
Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the toggle; activating a link closes it; resizing past the phone width resets it.
Sticky bars do not hide focus: scroll-padding keeps focused elements and anchor targets clear of the bar (WCAG 2.2 Focus Not Obscured).
Place a skip link before the bar so keyboard users can bypass the repeated links.
do: Keep four to six links; one primary call to action.
Put the skip link first.
Mark the current section with aria-current="page".
dont: Do not use it inside the app shell.
Do not add dropdown menus on hover; link to a section page instead.
Do not write aria-expanded without the behaviour or your own handler.

number-field.name: number-field
number-field.use: A number the user can type or step with minus and plus buttons (quantity, count, small ranges). For large ranges or free exploration use slider; for amounts with units use input-group.
number-field.states: disabled; a step button is aria-disabled at the min or max (it stays focusable); data-repeat on .number-field repeats while a button is held
number-field.notes: A native input type=number sits between two .btn--icon buttons marked data-step=-1 and data-step=1 (number-field behaviour). The native spinner is hidden; Arrow Up/Down, min, max, step and validity still come from the input. Buttons use step and clamp to min and max, set aria-disabled at a limit (not disabled, so focus is never lost), and announce "<label>: <value>" in a polite live region. Name the buttons (aria-label) and the input (a <label for> or aria-label). Use inputmode="decimal" and step="0.5" for decimals. data-repeat enables hold-to-repeat. React (0.19.0, proposal 055): NumberField renders this exact markup. Props: label (the input name, also used as "Decrease <label>" / "Increase <label>"; or labelledBy for a visible label), id, value / defaultValue (number or null for empty) and onChange(number | null), min, max, step, decimal, decrementLabel, incrementLabel, disabled, name. Controlled or uncontrolled. The buttons are aria-disabled at the limits, typing is clamped on blur, and a polite live region announces "<label>: <value>" after a button press. Hold-to-repeat is a plain-HTML feature (data-repeat) and is not in the React helper.
a11y: The input is a native spinbutton: Arrow Up/Down step it, Page Up/Down and typing work, min/max/step validation is the browser's.
The step buttons have names (Decrease quantity) and stay in the tab order; at a limit they are aria-disabled rather than disabled so focus is not dropped.
After a button changes the value, a polite live region announces "Quantity: 4"; hold-to-repeat announces once the value settles.
Out-of-range typing is clamped to min or max on change.
Both buttons are at least the control height (24 px minimum).
React NumberField has the same ARIA as the plain component: named buttons, aria-disabled (not disabled) at min and max, a polite status region, and a native spinbutton input.
do: Set min and max so the buttons stop at sensible limits.
Use inputmode numeric or decimal for phone keyboards.
dont: Do not use it for large ranges (age, year): use a plain input or select.
Do not use it for values the user needs to see in context (volume, brightness): use slider.

pagination.name: pagination
pagination.use: Moves through a long list or table that is split into pages. For a short list use infinite scroll or a "Show more" button; for steps through a process use steps. The page-jump variant suits a long document viewer or list where the user wants to type a page number.

mode: pagination--jump (previous, a "3 / 12" readout that becomes a number input, next)

pagination.states: aria-current="page" on the current page; aria-disabled="true" (links) or disabled (buttons) on an unavailable previous/next
pagination.markup: PreviousPage 3 of 121234…12Next
pagination.notes: A <nav class="pagination" aria-label="..."> holding links (server-rendered pages) or buttons (client-side pages) with class pagination__item, in this order: previous (data-step="prev"), .pagination__status, the numbers with .pagination__ellipsis where pages are skipped, next (data-step="next"). The nav is a size container, so it reacts to the space it is given, not the window: put it in a block-level parent (not directly in a flex row: wrap it in a div). Wide: Previous/Next with text. Below ~34rem the words become visually hidden (kept in the DOM, so the accessible name stays) and below ~28rem the numbers are replaced by the status text "Page 3 of 12". Keep the status element in the markup; it is hidden while the numbers are shown. A disabled end is a <span aria-disabled="true"> or a disabled <button>; do not leave a dead link. Show the first and last page, the current page and one neighbour on each side (react/Pagination does this with pageRange()). Pair with a page-size select and a result count by placing them in a .cluster above or beside the nav (see the example). Page-jump variant: add pagination--jump and use only three children in order: previous (data-step="prev", icon only, aria-label), the readout button (pagination__item pagination__jump showing "3 / 12", aria-label "Page 3 of 12", aria-description "Go to page") and next. There are no numbers, ellipsis or status text, so it stays on one line at any width. Activating the readout is a script concern (plain pages) or the jump prop (React): swap the button for input.input.pagination__input[type=number][min=1][max=N] with an aria-label such as "Go to page (1 to 12)", focus and select it; Enter applies a valid page, Escape and blur cancel; restore the readout and its focus afterwards. Use it for sequential browsing (a document viewer); keep the numbered form for tables.
a11y: A <nav> landmark with an aria-label ("Pages"); if a page has two paginations, label them differently.
The current page has aria-current="page" and a visible border, tint and heavier weight, not colour alone.
Each number has an accessible name (aria-label="Page 4"); the previous/next words stay in the DOM when they are visually hidden, so their names are kept.
A disabled end is aria-disabled (or disabled) and not a link; it is skipped by Tab when it is a disabled button.
In a narrow container the status "Page 3 of 12" replaces the numbers, so the position is still announced.
Targets are at least the control height (comfortable) or 24px (compact density).
Page jump: the previous/next icon buttons and the readout button have accessible names ("Previous page", "Page 3 of 12"); the readout also describes itself as "Go to page".
The jump input is a labelled number field with min and max; it is focused and selected when it opens, Enter applies, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the readout either way.
do: Always show first and last page and the current page.
Keep the page in the URL (links) so the back button and sharing work.
Move focus to the top of the results (or announce the update) after a client-side page change.
Use the page-jump variant for a viewer or long document where typing a page number is quicker than stepping.
dont: Do not use it for fewer than three pages.
Do not put it directly in a flex row; wrap it in a block container.
Do not remove the status element; narrow containers need it.
Do not mix the page-jump readout with page numbers in one nav.

progress.name: progress
progress.use: Progress of a task (upload, import, setup) with <progress>, or a measurement within a known range (disk, quota, score) with <meter>. Use loading when you cannot say how long it takes and there is nothing to measure.
progress.notes: Native elements, so value, max and the accessible role come for free. Always pair them with a visible label (<label for>) and show the number as text as well: the bar alone is a graphic, not a reading. Omit the value attribute for an indeterminate progress. For <meter> set min, max, low, high and optimum: the fill is green when the value is in the good range, amber in the middle and red in the worst range, which depends on where optimum lies (see the examples). The fill colour is never the only signal because the label and number are visible. Series colour (proposal 124): a progress fill reads --series, which data-series="1" to "8" (set on the progress or an ancestor, see chart) provides, so a bar can carry the colour of the series it stands for; without data-series it stays the accent. Name the series in text, never by colour alone.
a11y: <progress> exposes role=progressbar with its value and max; <meter> exposes role=meter. Give each a visible <label for> so the name is the same for everyone.
Show the value as text next to the bar; the fill length is not a substitute for it.
An indeterminate <progress> (no value) is announced as busy/unknown; add words like "Preparing..." in the label.
Meter colours come from the status text tokens and meet 3:1 against the track; the number and label carry the meaning, so colour is not the only signal.
Forced-colors mode falls back to the browser's native progress and meter rendering; reduced motion makes the indeterminate bar static.
do: Update the value as work advances; keep the label stable.
Use meter for values with a range (disk, quota) and progress for tasks.
Pair with the percentage or "x of y" text.
dont: Do not use progress for a value that is not about completion.
Do not use a bar without a label.
Do not fake progress; use indeterminate when unknown.

search.name: search
search.use: A search box with a leading icon, a clear button and a loading state. For choosing one value from a list as you type use combobox.
search.states: aria-busy=true on .search (loading), disabled on the input; the clear button shows only while the field has text
search.notes: Layout needs no script: the clear button is hidden by CSS while the input shows its placeholder (so a placeholder is required). The input-extras behaviour makes the clear button empty the field, fire input and change, and return focus. Put the search in a <form role="search"> (or <search>) with an accessible name. While results load set aria-busy="true" on .search: the clear button gives way to a spinner. Announce result counts in your own role=status region. React: the Search helper builds this markup. It takes every native input prop, requires placeholder and onClear (a controlled input must be emptied by your state, so the clear button calls onClear and then returns focus to the input), and offers clearLabel (default "Clear search"), busy (aria-busy on the wrapper), className (wrapper layout), inputClassName and inputRef. Without aria-label or aria-labelledby the placeholder names the input.
a11y: Use type=search with an accessible name (aria-label or a visible label); the icon is decorative.
Wrap the search in a form with role=search (or the <search> element) and a name so it is a landmark; if the page has several searches give each a distinct name.
The clear button is a real button named "Clear search"; after it empties the field focus returns to the input so typing can continue. Browsers' own cancel button is hidden so there is only one.
Loading is conveyed visually by a spinner and with aria-busy; announce the number of results in a role=status region yourself, as nothing here knows your data.
do: Search on input after a short debounce, or on Enter, but say which.
Keep the placeholder as an example of what can be searched.
dont: Do not hide the label from everyone: if there is no visible label, use aria-label.
Do not clear the field when the user presses Escape in a way that loses typed text without a way back.

segmented.name: segmented
segmented.use: Choosing one of a few options inline (view mode, period). More than five options or a value that is submitted with a form: use a select or radio choices.
segmented.states: aria-pressed="true" on the chosen item; disabled
segmented.notes: A group of toggle buttons that works from markup (behaviors.js, or the React Segmented): clicking an item sets aria-pressed on it and clears the others; add data-multiple to the group to let items toggle independently. Add data-value to an item for a stable value; the group emits design:change {item, value, pressed}. Wraps to a second row when the container is narrow. Count (0.23.0, proposal 072): put 3 after the label for a number such as unread items. It is small, tabular and inherits the item colour, so it is muted until the item is pressed. The React Segmented item takes a count prop.
a11y: Each item is a button (Tab to reach, Enter or Space to choose) with aria-pressed; the group has role=group and an aria-label that names the choice.
The chosen item is drawn raised and in full text colour, not by colour alone; in forced-colors mode it gets a Highlight border.
Pick-one is the default: choosing an item clears aria-pressed on the others for you; with data-multiple on the group the items toggle independently.
The count is part of the button text, so it is read after the label ("Unread 3"); the pressed state still comes from aria-pressed.
do: Keep labels to one or two words.
Always label the group.
dont: Do not use it for navigation between pages: use tabs.
Do not use it for more than about five options.

setting.name: setting
setting.use: A settings row: label and hint on the start side, one compact control (switch, select, number input, button) on the end side, with a divider between rows (add setting--plain to a row to drop the divider above it). For a label stacked over a control use field; for read-only facts use kv.
setting.states: none of its own; the control inside shows disabled, invalid and so on
setting.markup: How long the model stays loaded.
setting.notes: Put the rows of one group in a plain container (a card body or a stack); the divider is drawn between consecutive rows. The label is a real label for the control. A switch or a button keeps its own size, so give it no width step. When the container is narrow the control wraps under the text. React: <Setting label hint size>{id => <input id={id} className="input" />}</Setting>.
a11y: The label is a real label element tied to the control with for and id, so it names the control and enlarges its click target.
A hint is plain text next to the label; connect it with aria-describedby on the control when it explains a constraint.
A switch needs role="switch" and its label from the row; do not repeat the label in aria-label.
do: Use one control per row.
Keep the label to a short phrase and put the explanation in the hint.
dont: Do not put two or more controls in the control area; use a group of rows or a card.
Do not use it for a form with required fields and errors; use field.

shell.name: shell
shell.use: The page frame of every app: sidebar navigation, a top bar and the content column. Use it for apps and for documentation with a left-hand table of contents. A page without a sidebar (marketing site, landing page) uses navbar + content + site-footer instead.
shell.states: aria-current="page" on the active .nav-item (filled, accent bar, darker on hover); aria-pressed="true" on a .nav-item picked for a batch action (filled, no bar, darker on hover); data-nav="open" on .shell while the phone drawer is open; aria-expanded on the .menu-button
shell.markup:
Skip to content
App
Home
Home

Home
shell.notes: Landmarks: the sidebar is an <aside> that contains one <nav aria-label="Main"> (a second nav in the footer needs its own label); there is exactly one <main> (the .content element, with id="main" as the skip-link target) and one <h1> inside it. The first focusable element of the page is a .skip-link. Below 56rem the sidebar is an icon rail: keep an icon first in each nav item and wrap the text in .rail-hide (add a title attribute so the name shows on hover). Below 40rem it is a drawer: put <button class="btn btn--ghost btn--icon menu-button" aria-label="Open navigation" aria-controls="sidebar"> in the top bar, add an empty <div class="scrim" aria-hidden="true"> inside .shell and give the aside id="sidebar". Plain HTML pages include shell.js: it sets aria-expanded, moves focus into the drawer when it opens, makes the page behind it inert, keeps Tab inside, and on Escape, scrim click or a link click closes it and returns focus to the menu button. React apps own that state: set data-nav on .shell, aria-expanded on the button, and give .main the inert attribute while open. On a phone the topbar has room for about two breadcrumb levels (collapse longer trails with breadcrumb__more) or one .topbar__title. Topbar slots: put the menu button and the breadcrumb (or .topbar__title) first, then .topbar__actions for badges, search, the theme toggle and the user menu. .page-header holds the eyebrow, the h1, a .page-header__description line and the page's primary actions. A page without sidebar: <a class="skip-link">, <header class="navbar">, <main class="content" id="main">, <footer class="site-footer"> (see the last example). Plain pages can put a theme, accent and density switcher in the topbar with data-theme-control="mode|accent|density" on a button, a select and a button (behaviors.js with theme.js; React has ThemeToggle, useTheme and useDensity). .workspace gives a pane that holds a canvas, map or board a recessed background (--surface-muted) so it reads as a well against the chrome (topbar, toolbar--bar, sidebar), which stay on --surface. Put it on the pane that fills the area under the toolbar. The scrim also works outside the shell: data-open="true" on .scrim covers the page and dims it (used behind a side-panel's phone .sheet). Collapsible section: button.nav-item.nav-item--section[aria-expanded][aria-controls] (label first, a trailing chevron-right icon last) followed by a .nav-items group of .nav-item links (indented under a rule); hide a collapsed group with the hidden attribute. Nothing is remembered between visits and no script is provided: the page owns the expanded state. Sidebar roles (proposal 110): the left sidebar is where to go (the pages of a section and lists you switch between, as nav-section groups with an eyebrow heading) and has one scroll area, so several groups stack in one scrolling container and a group never scrolls on its own; the right panel (side-panel) is about what you are looking at (details, references, preview, inspector, table of contents), is collapsible, and holds nothing essential. data-collapsed="true" on .shell (proposal 150) gives the icon rail on a wide screen by the user's choice, the same layout as below 56rem: put the text that should disappear in .rail-hide, and keep the toggle button (with aria-expanded) and the remembered state in the app. The toggle (proposal 175) is always at the top right of the sidebar: a button.btn.btn--ghost.btn--icon.sidebar__toggle inside .sidebar__brand after the name (icon panel-left-close when expanded, panel-left-open when collapsed, aria-label Collapse sidebar / Expand sidebar). The sidebar never disappears completely: two states only, expanded and icon rail, switchable on every page. On a phone the drawer applies as before. Proposal 176: data-collapsed="false" (the user chose expanded) keeps the sidebar expanded between 40rem and 56rem instead of the automatic icon rail; leave the attribute off to keep the automatic rail there.
a11y: Landmarks: <aside> with a labelled <nav>, one <main id="main">, a banner/topbar header; screen-reader users can jump between them.
The skip link is the first Tab stop and moves focus past the sidebar to the main content.
The current page is marked with aria-current="page" (a visible bar plus a tinted background, not colour alone; in forced-colours mode an outline).

The phone drawer is out of the tab order and hidden from assistive technology while closed (visibility: hidden); when open, the page behind is inert, Tab stays in the drawer, Escape closes it and focus returns to the menu button.
The menu button exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls; the icon-only rail items keep their text in the DOM (hidden visually) so the accessible name stays.
brand-wordmark clips an svg: name it with role="img" and aria-label, or hide it with aria-hidden when the name is text elsewhere; the retract motion is removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
A collapsible section heading is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the chevron icon is decorative. In the icon rail the heading is hidden and its items stay reachable as links.
do: One <main> and one <h1> per page.
Give every nav item an icon so the icon rail stays usable.
Label each <nav> (Main, Breadcrumb, Legal) when a page has more than one.
Use .page-header__description for the one-line explanation of the page.
dont: Do not nest a second shell inside the content.
Do not use the topbar for page navigation that belongs in the sidebar.
Do not hide the menu button on phones; it is the only way into the drawer.
Do not put the whole page title only in the topbar; the h1 belongs in the content.

side-panel.name: side-panel
side-panel.use: The surface of a non-modal panel that sits beside the main content (a right-hand inspector, tools or preview column), plus its phone form: a bottom sheet over a scrim. Use the shell sidebar for navigation, a drawer for a modal sheet and a card for content inside the page.
side-panel.states: data-open="true" on .sheet shows it (closed it is hidden and out of the tab order); data-open="true" on .scrim dims the page behind it
side-panel.markup:
......
...
side-panel.notes: side-panel is only a surface: a muted background and a hairline on the inline-start edge, with no size, position or scrolling. The project's layout (an app-* class) gives it its width and height and the toggle that collapses it. On a phone render a .sheet instead: a bottom sheet (fixed, up to 85% of the viewport height, scrolls inside) with an optional .sheet__handle grab bar; set data-open="true" to open it and put a .scrim (data-open="true") before it to dim the page. The app owns the state: open and close, Escape, focus return and inert on the page behind (the sheet is not a native dialog; use Drawer when a modal sheet is enough). The scrim class belongs to shell; inside .shell the scrim keeps its drawer behaviour (data-nav on the shell); data-open on a scrim is the form for use outside the shell. The collapse and expand buttons use the icons panel-right-close and panel-right-open. Role (proposal 110): the right panel is about what you are looking at (details, references, preview, inspector, table of contents). It is collapsible (a bottom sheet on phones), so it is never the only way to reach a page and holds nothing essential. Navigation belongs in the left sidebar (shell), which has one scroll area.
a11y: Give the panel or sheet an accessible name (aria-label on the <aside>); it is a complementary landmark.
The sheet is not modal by itself: the app moves focus into it when it opens, returns it to the opener on close and makes the page behind inert while the scrim shows.
A closed sheet is visibility: hidden, so it is out of the tab order and hidden from assistive technology.
The grab handle is decoration (aria-hidden); provide a visible close or collapse button.
The slide is removed with prefers-reduced-motion; borders switch to system colours in forced-colors mode.
do: Use side-panel for a panel that stays beside the content.
Use the sheet and the scrim on a phone, where a column beside the content does not fit.
dont: Do not style the panel's width or position in the system; do that in your own app-* layout class.
Do not use the sheet for a short decision (use a modal) or navigation (use the shell sidebar).

site-footer.name: site-footer
site-footer.use: The footer of a website: secondary link columns and the legal row (copyright, imprint, privacy). Apps with a shell do not need it; they use .sidebar__footer.
site-footer.markup:
Product

  • Pricing

© 2026 Company

site-footer.notes:

directly in is the page's contentinfo landmark. .site-footer__columns holds .site-footer__column blocks (an h2.site-footer__title and a plain

sizer.name: sizer
sizer.use: Keeps the width of a live value stable: the box is as wide as the widest value it can take, so neighbouring controls do not move when the number changes. Use it for counters, readouts and statuses that update while the page is open.
sizer.states: The second child is aria-hidden="true"; it is only there to reserve width.
sizer.notes: Two children in one grid cell: the visible value first, then an aria-hidden copy of the widest text it can take (for example the total repeated: "500 / 500"). The hidden copy is invisible (visibility: hidden) and removed from the accessibility tree. Compute the widest text from the data (the number of digits of the maximum), never a fixed pixel width. React: <Sizer widest="500 / 500">85 / 500</Sizer>.
a11y: The hidden copy has aria-hidden="true" so screen readers read the value once.
Do not put interactive content in the hidden copy.
do: Build the hidden copy from the widest value the data can reach.
Use it for every number that updates while the user watches.
dont: Do not use it to force equal widths of static text.
Do not give the hidden copy a different font or size from the visible text.

skip-link.name: skip-link
skip-link.use: A link that lets keyboard and screen-reader users jump over repeated navigation to the main content (WCAG 2.4.1). Every page with a sidebar or navbar needs one.
skip-link.states: visible only while it has keyboard focus
skip-link.notes: Make it the first focusable element in <body> and give the <main> element id="main" (a target that is not focusable is fine in current browsers; add tabindex="-1" for older ones). The link slides in at the top inline-start corner when it is focused.
a11y: It is a real link: Enter follows it, and focus lands in the target region so the next Tab starts inside the content.
It is off screen (not display:none) until focused, so it is in the tab order from the start and screen readers can reach it.
When focused it has a solid accent background, readable text (on-accent) and an outline that works in every theme and in forced-colours mode.
do: Put it first in the DOM, before the sidebar or navbar.
Use a short label: "Skip to content" (or "Zum Inhalt springen").
dont: Do not hide it with display:none or visibility:hidden.
Do not add more than one or two skip links.

slider.name: slider
slider.use: Picking a value inside a known range where the position matters more than the exact number (volume, opacity, price band). If the exact number matters use number-field.
slider.states: disabled; --slider-fill is set by the behaviour (the filled part of the track)
slider.markup: 40
slider.notes: A native input type=range with class slider. The input-extras behaviour sets --slider-fill so the track shows the chosen part (Firefox draws it natively; without the behaviour the thumb alone shows the value), updates every <output for=<id>>, and with data-unit="%" also sets aria-valuetext. Min/max labels go in .slider__scale (aria-hidden: the values are already in the input). Two sliders can form a range: data-lte="#other" on the lower and data-gte="#other" on the upper keep them in order. The thumb is 24 px for touch. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem the input is 44px high so the thumb can be grabbed in a 44px band (track and thumb keep their size).
a11y: A native range input: Arrow keys step, Home/End jump to the ends, Page Up/Down step by larger amounts; it is announced as a slider with its value.
Give it a visible <label for>. The <output> shows the value as text, so the value is not only a position; with data-unit the unit is part of aria-valuetext.
The thumb is 24 px, so it is easy to hit by touch; the focus ring surrounds the control and the thumb.
In forced-colors mode the track and thumb use system colours.
do: Show the current value as text next to the slider.
Label the ends when the scale is not obvious.
dont: Do not use a slider for precise input such as a year: use number-field.
Do not rely on the thumb position alone to communicate the value.

split.name: split
split.use: Two resizable panes with a draggable, keyboard-operable handle: viewer and properties, editor and preview, list and detail. The handle resizes the first pane.

size: split--fill (the height of a bounded parent, both directions)

split.states: data-size on .split is the starting size of the first pane in percent (default 50). On the handle: data-min and data-max (percent, default 10 and 90), data-step (default 2) and data-big-step (default 10), data-collapsible. data-dragging is set while dragging. The collapsed pane is inert.
split.markup:
First pane

Second pane
split.notes: Markup: .split > .split__pane + .split__handle[role=separator] + .split__pane. The handle needs an aria-label, aria-controls (the first pane id), aria-orientation (vertical for side by side, horizontal for stacked), and aria-valuenow/min/max (split.js keeps them current; the static values are the no-script fallback). Sizes are percentages of the split. split.js writes ONE runtime custom property, --split-size, on the .split element (the first pane's size, e.g. 40%); it persists nothing, so remember the size yourself from the design:resize event (detail {size, collapsed}) if you want to. The side-by-side form needs no height; .split--vertical has a default height of 24rem, so give it a height from layout (height or flex) in a real page. Below the small breakpoint the side-by-side form stacks its panes and hides the handle (use .split--vertical if the user must be able to resize on phones). Panes scroll on their own (overflow auto) and may contain any content; make the inner content a layout of its own. Right-to-left: the first pane sits at the inline start and the Left/Right keys are mirrored. React: <Split first={...} second={...} defaultSize={40} min={15} max={85} collapsible label="Resize panes" />. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem the handle's invisible drag area is 44px wide (or high when vertical). split--fill (React: fill) makes the split take the height of a parent that has one (a flex or grid cell with min-height 0), for a full-height workspace such as media bin | preview | inspector over a timeline.
a11y: The handle is a focusable role="separator" (the window splitter pattern) with aria-orientation, aria-controls, aria-label and aria-valuenow/min/max in percent.

Keyboard: Left/Right (Up/Down when stacked) move one step, Shift moves a big step, Home and End go to the minimum and maximum, Enter collapses and restores a data-collapsible pane. Left and Right are mirrored in right-to-left.
Pointer: drag with mouse, pen or touch (touch-action is none on the handle); double-click resets to the starting size. The hit area is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
A collapsed pane is inert (not focusable, hidden from assistive technology) and the handle reports aria-valuenow 0.
Below the small breakpoint the panes stack in reading order; the handle is hidden unless the split is .split--vertical.
In forced-colors mode the handle line is drawn in CanvasText and Highlight when active.
do: Give the handle a label that names what it resizes.
Set data-min so a pane never becomes unusable.
Offer data-collapsible for secondary panes.
dont: Do not nest more than two levels of splits.
Do not rely on dragging only; the keyboard path is part of the component.
Do not set --split-size yourself except in the stylesheet for a first paint.

stat.name: stat
stat.use: Deprecated: use stat-strip (stat-strip--lg for a headline number, stat-strip--cards for tiles). A headline number with a label. For charts use the data-viz components.

A change next to the stat (a badge) says the direction in words or a sign (+12% vs last week); the tone colour is only reinforcement.

Use grid--compact to lay out a strip.
Keep the label short.
dont: Do not use stat for text that is not a metric.
Do not animate the number on every update.
