a11y: A description list: each label is paired with its value for assistive technology.
Give the list an aria-label that says what the numbers are.
Values that update often should not be live regions; announce only important changes elsewhere.
While a value loads set aria-busy="true" on its item and expose a polite status message; skeletons are decorative.
A change next to a value (a badge) says the direction in words or a sign (+12% vs last week); the tone colour is only reinforcement.
do: Keep labels to one or two words.
Use sizer for numbers that change.
Show units and the comparison period in the label.
dont: Do not use more than about six readouts in a row; use a table or kv.
Do not use it for text that is not a metric.
Do not animate the number on every update.

steps.name: steps
steps.use: Shows progress through a fixed sequence such as a wizard, checkout or onboarding. It displays state; the Back/Next buttons and the step content are separate.
steps.states: data-state="complete" | "upcoming" on .steps__item; aria-current="step" on the current item
steps.markup:
1. Account (completed)
  2. 2ProjectStep 2 of 3
  3. 3Review
steps.notes:
An
    of
  1. . Each item has a .steps__marker (aria-hidden: a number, or the check icon for a complete step), a .steps__label and an optional .steps__description. State uses attributes, not classes: data-state="complete" (marker shows ; add (completed) inside the label), aria-current="step" on the one current item, data-state="upcoming" (or nothing) on the rest. Put Step 2 of 5 inside the current item: it stays hidden normally, and when the container is narrower than 40rem the horizontal stepper collapses to the current step plus that text. The vertical variant never collapses. Steps is a size container: place it in a block-level parent. Steps are not clickable by default; if earlier steps can be revisited make the label a link or button inside the item.
a11y: An ordered list with an accessible name; the current step is aria-current="step".
A complete step shows a check icon and has "(completed)" in visually hidden text; upcoming steps differ by a muted marker and text. Colour is never the only signal.
Markers are aria-hidden (the number repeats the list position); the label carries the name.
When the container is narrow, the visible text "Step 2 of 5" (a real text node) replaces the other items so position is still conveyed.
In forced-colours mode complete markers use Highlight/HighlightText and the current marker gets a thicker border.
do: Keep labels to one to three words.
Mark exactly one item aria-current="step" while the process runs.
Put the status text in the current item.
dont: Do not use steps for navigation between unrelated pages; use tabs or the navbar.
Do not use more than about seven steps.
Do not rely on the marker colour to show completion.

switch.name: switch
switch.use: An on/off setting that takes effect immediately. Use a checkbox (choice) for options that are submitted with a form.
switch.markup: <label class="cluster cluster--sm"><input type="checkbox" role="switch" class="switch"> Auto-restart</label>
switch.notes: It is a real checkbox with role=switch, so it works in forms, with the keyboard (Space) and with autofill-free semantics. The knob moves in the reading direction (flips in right-to-left). Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem an invisible 44px box around the track is the tap target (the track keeps its size).
a11y: role=switch on a checkbox is announced as a switch with state on or off; Space toggles it, as for any checkbox.
Every switch needs a visible label (wrap it in a <label> or use for/id); in a settings row use aria-labelledby.
The state is shown by position as well as by colour (the knob moves), and by the accent fill; in forced-colors mode the track uses Highlight.
A switch applies immediately. If the change needs a Save button, use a checkbox instead.
do: Phrase the label as the thing being turned on (Notifications), not as an action.
Apply the change at once and confirm it if it is slow.
dont: Do not use a switch inside a form that is submitted later: use a checkbox.
Do not change the label text when toggled; the state is the switch's job.

table.name: table
table.use: Tabular data with several columns to compare. Wrap in .table-wrap so it scrolls on narrow screens. For a single column of items use list; for key/value pairs use kv.

layout: rules-strong (darker lines between body rows, for dense lists beside a chart or with many similar rows)
fixed (keeps column widths stable as rows load; remaining columns share available width)
framed wrapper (closed, softly rounded box: faint frame on all sides, dark column titles, grouped tbody blocks stay separated; also with a scrolling wrapper and sticky header)
stacked (rows become cards on a phone)
row-actions (action cells appear on row hover or focus; always visible on touch)
footer (table-wrap__foot under a table-wrap__scroll: page size, result count, pagination; the scroll part fills the height, the foot stays visible)

table.states: th[aria-sort=ascending|descending|none] on sortable headers; tr[aria-selected="true"] on selected rows; aria-busy="true" on a loading tbody; table--stacked: below the phone breakpoint each row is a card and td[data-label] shows its column title; table--row-actions: .table__actions cells shown on tr:hover, tr:focus-within (keyboard) or while a control inside has aria-expanded="true"; always shown on touch screens (hover: none)
table.notes: Native table semantics only: caption, thead/tbody, th with scope implied. Cell padding follows density (--density-y/x). Add table--fixed when column widths must stay stable as rows change; numeric and action columns stay compact, and remaining columns share the available width. Sortable: add data-sortable to the table, put a button.table__sort (label + sort icon) in each sortable th and set aria-sort on the th; table.js does the rest. The icon class should match the state (icon--arrow-up-down none, icon--arrow-up ascending, icon--arrow-down descending) so server-rendered markup is right before any script runs. Selectable: first cell of each row is .table__select with a checkbox; the header checkbox is select-all. Sticky header needs a height-bounded .table-wrap (.table-wrap--scroll, or height/max-height from the project layout CSS). A scrollable wrap should have tabindex="0", role="region" and an aria-label so keyboard users can scroll it. Stacked (0.19.0, proposal 053): add table--stacked and give every td (or th scope="row") a data-label with its column title. At phone width (below 40rem) the header row is visually hidden (still read by screen readers), each tr becomes a bordered card and each cell shows its data-label above the value; wider than that the table is unchanged. Numeric, centred, select and action cells align to the start in the card and are as wide as their content (table--fixed column widths are cancelled, so table--fixed + table--stacked is safe); the actions cell is a wrapping row of buttons, no project class needed. Do not combine with table--sticky. Keep the .table-wrap: it has nothing to scroll on a phone but keeps the wide layout safe. Because display is changed on table elements, add role="table", "rowgroup", "row", "columnheader" and "cell" for assistive technology that drops table semantics from display: block (older Safari). Framed (0.22.0, proposal 084): add table-wrap--framed to the .table-wrap of a dense data table that reads as one closed box. The normal (faint) border frames all four sides with rounded corners (the header gets the same line above and below), column titles use the full text colour, and when the table has several tbody blocks (grouped rows) the last row of each block keeps its bottom line so groups do not run together. Because the frame is on the wrapper it also works when the wrapper scrolls: combine with table-wrap--scroll (or a height from the project layout CSS) and table--sticky for a bounded table whose header stays visible. Combine with table--grid for column rules. Row actions (0.23.0, proposals 083 and 069, the same mechanism as list__actions--hover): add table--row-actions to the table so the .table__actions cells stay transparent until the row is hovered or a control inside it has focus (:focus-within). The buttons stay in the tab order (opacity only), and touch screens, which cannot hover, always show them. Keep the "Actions" column title as sr-only text. React tables that own their sort state use the SortableHeader helper (th[aria-sort] > button.table__sort with the matching arrow icon) instead of data-sortable. Strong row rules (0.26.0): add table--rules-strong to draw the lines between body rows with the strong border instead of the faint one; the header line is unchanged. It combines with table--sticky, table--grid and table-wrap--framed. Footer (proposal 146): put the table in .table-wrap__scroll (it carries role="region", tabindex="0" and the aria-label, and is the only part that scrolls) and add .table-wrap__foot as the next child of .table-wrap: a bar with a top border holding the page-size select, the result count ("Showing 1-25 of 170") and a nav.pagination (in a block-level div, since the nav is a size container). The wrapper becomes a flex column and clips to its frame; give it a height from the project layout CSS (or let a flex parent size it) and the scroll part shrinks while the foot stays visible.
a11y: A real <table> with <caption> (or aria-label) and <th> header cells gives screen readers row and column context; never build tables from divs.
A sortable header is a <button> inside the <th>; Enter and Space sort. aria-sort on the th announces the current sort, and table.js adds a polite live region message ("Sorted by Name, ascending").
Sort direction is shown by an arrow icon, not by colour or opacity alone.
Row checkboxes need an accessible name that includes the row (aria-label="Select Atlas"); the header checkbox is "Select all" and becomes indeterminate when only some rows are selected.
Selected rows set aria-selected="true" and also have a checked checkbox, so selection is never colour only; in forced-colors mode they use Highlight.
A horizontally scrollable wrap is focusable (tabindex="0") with a role and name so keyboard users can scroll it.
Icon-only row action buttons carry an aria-label that names the row.

table--stacked keeps the real table markup. The hidden header row stays in the accessibility tree and the visible labels come from data-label, so the same column title is read once. Add the table roles listed in the notes for browsers that drop table semantics from display: block elements. Controls inside cells keep their own names and tab order, which stays in reading order.

With table--row-actions the action buttons are only made transparent: they stay in the tab order with their aria-labels, focus inside the row reveals them (:focus-within), and touch screens always show them.
do: Right-align numbers (table__num) and keep units in the header.
Keep one sortable column active at a time and show it.
Give every table a caption or label.
Use an empty state row instead of an empty body.
Use table--stacked for editable or wide data tables that must work at 390px; give every td a data-label.
Use table--row-actions for dense tables with per-row edit/delete icons.
dont: Do not use a table for layout.
Do not hide the header on small screens yourself; use table--stacked (labels per cell) or let the wrap scroll.
Do not put long paragraphs or forms inside cells.
Do not rely on row colour alone to show selection or status.
Do not hide row actions with display or visibility in project CSS; use table--row-actions.

tabs.name: tabs
tabs.use: Switching between views of the same content, one panel visible at a time. With the closable variant it also switches between open documents or projects in an editor (close, new, rename, unsaved marker). For navigation between pages use nav items or a navbar; for filtering a list use the segmented control.

layout: (wraps: the panel drops below the list on narrow containers)
tabs-layout--responsive-flush (fills a bounded pane with no gap and no wrapping; below 56rem the side list becomes a horizontal bar; React: responsiveFlush)
closable: tabs--closable (horizontal: each tab sits in a .tabs__item with a .tabs__close button; the list and a .tabs-bar__new button sit in a .tabs-bar)
marker: data-modified on a tab (unsaved dot; also put "unsaved changes" in the tab's aria-label)
group: tabs__group (vertical only: a heading label between tabs)
rename: data-rename on the list (F2 or double-click swaps the tab for an input)

tabs.states: aria-selected="true" on the active tab; disabled / aria-disabled="true" on an unavailable tab; hidden on inactive panels; data-modified on a tab for unsaved changes
tabs.markup:
First panel
Second panel
tabs.notes:
Pattern: a .tabs[role=tablist] with a label, button.tab[role=tab] children, and one .tab-panel[role=tabpanel] per tab, after the list (in the same parent), in the same order. js/behaviors/tabs.js (plain HTML) or react/Tabs does the rest: roving tabindex, arrow keys (Left/Right; Up/Down when vertical), Home/End, aria-controls and aria-labelledby, toggling the panels' hidden attribute and a design:change event ({tab, panel, index}). Give tabs an id and write aria-controls yourself if the page must work without script. data-activation="manual" on the list switches to manual activation (use it when showing a panel is slow). data-hash on the list stores the selected tab's id in the URL hash and selects the tab named by an incoming #hash. Vertical tabs: wrap the .tabs--vertical list and its panel in .tabs-layout; the panel drops below the list on narrow containers. For a side list that fills a bounded pane, such as a dialog with a provider list on the left and its content and footer on the right, use .tabs-layout.tabs-layout--responsive-flush (React: the responsiveFlush prop) inside a flex or grid parent that has a height: no gap, no wrapping, and the visible panel is a column so a body can scroll inside it (below 56rem the list becomes a bar above the panel). Horizontal tabs with icons use a small gap between the icon and label. Each vertical tab is a flex row: put an optional leading .icon (turns accent when selected), the label, and an optional trailing .badge (a count, pushed to the end) inside the button; the selected row has a filled background and a 2px accent bar on its start edge. A tab bar wider than its container scrolls sideways and fades the clipped edge. Existing markup (tabs without panels, used as a view switcher by the app) keeps working: the behaviour only wires panels it can find. A panel in a height-bounded flex column (a dock or side pane) can take the remaining height and scroll inside it with the fill layout helper:
. Touch (0.19.1): on a coarse pointer or below 40rem every tab (horizontal and vertical) is at least 44px high (`--layout-control`); the bar still scrolls sideways. Closable (0.25.0, replaces project-tabs): put class tabs--closable on the tablist, wrap each tab in
followed by its close button (class "tabs__close btn btn--ghost btn--icon btn--sm", tabindex="-1", aria-hidden="true", and an aria-label naming the tab), and put the list plus a new-tab button (class "tabs-bar__new btn btn--ghost btn--icon btn--sm") in a
. The close button stays outside the tab button (a button must not contain a button) and is pointer-only: keyboard users press Delete on the focused tab. The behaviour finds the panels after the .tabs-bar, so keep them siblings of the bar. Unsaved changes: data-modified on the tab draws a dot; repeat the state in text (aria-label="Name.svg, unsaved changes"). Rename (data-rename on the list): F2 or double-click replaces the tab with an .input in its item; mark the label element with data-label (otherwise the tab's whole text is the label). Closable tabs are horizontal only. React: Tabs accepts onClose, onCreate, onRename, newLabel, modifiedLabel, className and panelClassName; items may carry icon, suffix and modified; pass children instead of item panels to share one panel across all tabs (an editor that switches documents). After a close, focus moves to the selected neighbour or the new-tab button; after an add that the page selects, focus moves to the new tab. Group heading: in a vertical list put Parsers between tabs as a direct child of the tab list; it is a label, not a tab (no tabindex, skipped by roving tabindex and the arrow keys, owns no panel, so keep the panels in tab order without it). It uses the eyebrow type in the muted colour, and is not shown in a horizontal list or in the bar a responsive flush list becomes below 56rem. React: an item of { group: "Parsers" } in items (it is dropped when the list is horizontal or narrow). The panel owns the space under the tab bar: .tab-panel has padding-block of --space-4, so content sits 16px below the bar (proposal 120).
a11y: role=tablist / tab / tabpanel with aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby; the list has an accessible name.
Roving tabindex: only the selected tab is in the Tab order; Tab then moves into the panel (panels without focusable content get tabindex=0).
Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tabs and wrap; Home/End jump to the first and last; right-to-left swaps the horizontal arrows.
Automatic activation selects on focus; manual activation selects with Enter or Space. Disabled tabs are skipped.

The selected tab differs by weight, text colour and a 2px accent line (vertical tabs also get a filled row), not colour alone; in forced-colours mode the selection is outlined in the Highlight colour.
design:change fires when the user changes the selection, so apps can react (load data, update the URL).

Closable: Delete on a focused tab closes it (aria-keyshortcuts="Delete"); the pointer-only close button is aria-hidden with tabindex -1, so it never doubles the tab stops. After closing, focus moves to a neighbouring tab or the new-tab button.
A .tabs__group heading is role=presentation and not focusable; screen readers may read it in passing, and arrow keys never land on it.
Renaming: F2 or double-click opens a labelled input; Enter or blur commits, Escape cancels and returns focus to the tab.
An unsaved tab carries the state in its accessible name ("Untitled.svg, unsaved changes"); the dot is decoration and is drawn in the system text colour in forced-colours mode.
do: Label the tab list (aria-label) and keep tab labels short.
Keep the panel order the same as the tab order.
Use data-activation="manual" when a panel is expensive to show.
Use tabs--closable for open documents or projects; keep the close button beside the tab, not inside it.
Include the unsaved state in the tab's accessible name as well as the dot.
Let the panel provide the space under the tab bar (.tab-panel pads 16px, --space-4, top and bottom). Start the panel content directly; do not add padding or margin above it.
dont: Do not use tabs for page navigation between URLs; use nav items or the navbar.
Do not nest tabs inside tabs.
Do not hide a tab; disable it and say why in its label or title.
Do not use closable tabs for URL navigation or ordinary sections; use nav items or plain tabs.
Do not put the close button inside the tab button.

Do not set padding, padding-block or margin with a top value other than var(--space-4) or 0 on a class passed as panelClassName, and do not wrap panel content in another box that pads its top. A page that needs a dense panel uses data-density="compact", not its own number.

tag-input.name: tag-input
tag-input.use: Free-text tags or keywords typed by the user (labels, recipients, keywords). When values must come from a fixed list use combobox with data-multiple.
tag-input.states: aria-invalid=true on the input (a refused tag), aria-disabled on the container, data-* settings for the behaviour
tag-input.markup: design
tag-input.notes: A container that looks like an input holding badge chips and one text box. Add data-tag-input to switch the behaviour on (tag-input behaviour; React: <TagInput>): Enter or comma adds, pasted text is split on commas, semicolons, tabs and new lines, Backspace in an empty box removes the last tag, and every chip has a remove button. Settings as attributes on .tag-input: data-name (hidden inputs for form submit), data-pattern (regular expression), data-max, data-duplicates (allow), data-add-on-blur. A refused tag stays in the box, the box gets aria-invalid="true" and design:invalid {value, reason: pattern|duplicate|max|rejected} fires; a page can also veto with a cancelable design:beforeadd {value}. design:change {values} fires after every change. Show the error text next to the field in your own handler. Added and removed tags are announced in a polite status region (translate with data-text-added, data-text-removed, data-text-invalid, data-text-remove).
a11y: The text box has an accessible name (a <label for> pointing at it, or aria-label); the container is only a visual frame.

Enter or comma adds the tag, Backspace in the empty box removes the last tag, Tab moves on; every chip has its own remove button, named "Remove <tag>", reachable by Tab, with a 24 px target (44 px wide on touch devices).

Adding, removing and refusing a tag are announced through a polite role=status region; a refused tag is also marked with aria-invalid on the box, and the page shows the reason as text linked with aria-describedby.
The focus ring is drawn on the text box and the whole control turns accent; the invalid state changes the border and needs the error text, not colour alone.
do: Say in the hint how tags are separated and which format is allowed.
Show the reason when a tag is refused.
dont: Do not use it for choosing from a fixed list: use combobox.
Do not rely on Backspace as the only way to remove: the remove buttons are there.

thumb.name: thumb
thumb.use: A frame that crops a picture or video poster to fill it without stretching, for cards in a gallery, a file picker or a media library. For a round picture of a person use avatar; for a picture inside running text use a plain img.
thumb.notes: span.thumb > img (or video) with width and height 100% and object-fit: cover, so every picture fills the frame whatever its shape and the frame never changes shape. The ratio comes from --thumb-ratio; the two modifiers set it, a project does not set it. The frame inherits the radius of its parent, so put it first inside a card and the card clips it. Set loading="lazy" on pictures below the fold (React Thumb does this and sets decoding="async"). A duration or type label on a thumbnail is a badge placed by the project's own layout class. An empty alt is right when the card title next to the picture names it.
a11y: The frame is a plain span with no role; the img inside carries the text alternative.
Use alt="" when the card title beside the picture already names it, otherwise describe the picture.
Cropping can hide part of a picture; do not put text that must be read inside a picture that is shown as a thumbnail.
do: Use the same ratio for every thumbnail in one grid.
Put the frame first inside a card so the card's radius clips it.
dont: Do not set a height or aspect-ratio of your own on the frame.
Do not use it for a person's picture; use avatar.

toast.name: toast
toast.use: A short confirmation or error that appears and goes away, for the result of something the user just did ("Saved", "Could not upload"). Use an alert for a message that belongs to the page, and a banner for a page-wide state that stays.
toast.states: role=status (polite) for neutral, success, warning and info; role=alert for errors; data-leaving while it fades out
toast.markup: Saved.
toast.notes: Plain pages: window.designToast.show({ message, tone, action: { label, onClick }, position }) (js/behaviors/toast.js) creates the stack and keeps at most designToast.max (4) toasts. React: ToastProvider once, useToast() anywhere: push(message, "success" | "error", action). All toasts dismiss after four seconds unless dismissed earlier. The stack is a labelled polite live region, errors inside it are role=alert. Never put the only copy of important information in a toast: it disappears. The fade respects prefers-reduced-motion. React ToastProvider takes labels={{ dismiss, region }} (proposal 152) so the dismiss button and the notifications region can be translated; the defaults stay English.
a11y: The stack is a region labelled "Notifications" and a polite live region: new toasts are announced without taking focus. Errors use role=alert and are announced immediately.
Every toast dismisses after four seconds unless dismissed earlier.
Every toast has a Dismiss button (icon with aria-label); Escape on a focused toast dismisses it.
Colour is never the only signal: the message states the result, and the tone border sits next to text. Motion is removed with prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Say what happened in a few words.
Offer Undo for reversible actions instead of asking first.
dont: Do not use a toast for something the user must read or act on later; use an alert or alert--banner.
Do not stack more than three or four at once.

tool-rail.name: tool-rail
tool-rail.use: A narrow rail of square tool buttons beside a canvas, map or board: run controls, drawing tools, a palette of building blocks. For a row of tools under a topbar use toolbar--bar; for a few icon buttons in a box use toolbar.
tool-rail.states: aria-pressed="true" on the active tool; disabled
tool-rail.notes: Put a vertical .toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-orientation=vertical) inside .tool-rail: toolbar.js then gives the whole rail one tab stop with arrow-key movement. Every cell is a btn (btn--primary for the main action, btn--ghost for tools) with .tool-rail__item. The picture is an .icon or a .tool-rail__glyph; a key hint (kbd) or a small badge sits in the corner with .tool-rail__key. Name the tool with aria-label and the hover title; the corner key is decoration. Divide groups with .toolbar__separator. React: <ToolRail label> with <ToolRailGroup label cols> and <ToolRailItem label keyHint badge icon glyph pressed variant>.
a11y: The rail is a toolbar: one tab stop, arrow keys move between tools, Home and End jump to the ends; separators and groups are announced.
Each tool has an accessible name (aria-label); the corner key is decoration and the shortcut is also given in the title.
The active tool is exposed with aria-pressed and a visible pressed style that is not colour only.
Cells are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
do: Give every tool a title with its name and shortcut.
Group related tools and divide groups with a separator.
Keep the rail to one or two columns.
dont: Do not put labels under the icons: the rail is narrow; use the title.
Do not mix text buttons and square cells in one grid.
Do not use it for a row of tools under a topbar (use toolbar--bar).

toolbar.name: toolbar
toolbar.use: A row of related controls (icon buttons, toggles, a segmented choice, a select) that is a single tab stop and is navigated with the arrow keys. Use it for editor, viewer and table tools; use plain buttons in a cluster for ordinary actions.

shape: toolbar--bar (edge to edge, square, bottom border only, padding at both ends)

toolbar.states: aria-orientation="vertical" on the toolbar stacks it. Toggle buttons use aria-pressed. disabled controls are skipped by the arrow keys.
toolbar.notes: Markup: .toolbar[role=toolbar][aria-label] with .toolbar__group (role=group + aria-label) and .toolbar__separator[role=separator]. Controls are btn btn--ghost btn--icon btn--sm (icon-only buttons need aria-label), toggle buttons with aria-pressed, a .segmented group, a .select (needs aria-label), or links. toolbar.js makes the toolbar one tab stop (roving tabindex): Left/Right (Up/Down for aria-orientation=vertical; mirrored in right-to-left) move between enabled controls, Home and End jump to the ends, Tab leaves the toolbar. Text inputs keep their own arrow keys, so avoid putting more than one in a toolbar. Controls inherit density: heights come from --layout-control-sm. React: <Toolbar label="..."> with <ToolbarGroup> and <ToolbarSeparator>. toolbar--bar turns the box into a full-width bar: no radius, no side borders, only a bottom border, and padding at both ends. Use it for the row of tools directly under a topbar; keep the default box for tools floating inside a pane.
a11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label; groups use role="group" with a label; separators are role="separator".

One tab stop (roving tabindex): Tab enters on the last used control, Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between enabled controls, Home and End jump to the first and last, Tab leaves. Disabled controls are skipped. Directions mirror in right-to-left.
Toggle buttons expose aria-pressed and a visible pressed style that is not colour only (tint, text colour and an underline bar); in forced-colors mode a Highlight border.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label; targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels in both densities.
Narrow screens: the default toolbar wraps onto more lines; .toolbar--scroll keeps one line and scrolls sideways (it stays reachable by keyboard because focus scrolls controls into view).
do: Group related tools and separate groups with a separator.
Keep the order stable between states; disable instead of removing.
dont: Do not put primary page actions in a toolbar.
Do not mix more than one text input in a toolbar.
Do not use it for navigation (use tabs or nav).

tooltip.name: tooltip
tooltip.use: A short text hint on an icon button or truncated text. Never the only place for essential information, and never for interactive content (use a popover for that).
tooltip.states: data-tip-dismissed (set by Escape), data-tip-open (touch tap), data-tip-side / data-tip-shift (set by tooltip.js)
tooltip.notes: Works with CSS alone for hover and keyboard focus. js/behaviors/tooltip.js makes it WCAG 1.4.13 compliant (Escape dismisses it, the pointer can move onto it without it vanishing, it stays until hover or focus leaves) and flips it at viewport edges; author a preferred side with data-tip-placement. The text is visual only: keep the control's own accessible name (aria-label or visible text). React: Tooltip wraps a control, renders a real description and wires aria-describedby. Text only, one short sentence; long text wraps at 24rem. React Tooltip takes align="start" or "end" (written as data-tip-shift) to line the bubble up with the control's edge when centring would clip it; a bubble is still drawn inside the control, so an ancestor with overflow clip or hidden can crop it (proposal 128 asked for a top-layer mode; not added).
a11y: Keyboard focus shows the tip as well as hover (WCAG 1.4.13 content on hover or focus).
Dismissible: Escape hides it without moving focus; it comes back on the next hover or focus.
Hoverable and persistent: the pointer can move onto the tip, and it stays until hover and focus leave. There is no timer.
The tip text is not exposed as the control's name or description by CSS alone: keep aria-label or visible text. The React Tooltip adds aria-describedby to a real description element.
Touch: a tap shows the tip, a tap elsewhere hides it. Tips never appear for controls that need the text to be understood.
do: Describe an icon-only action in two or three words.
Keep the control's aria-label identical to the tip text or shorter.
dont: Do not put links, buttons or essential instructions in a tooltip.
Do not use a tooltip on mobile as the only explanation; show a visible label instead.

tree.name: tree
tree.use: A hierarchy the user can expand, collapse and select from: file trees, document outlines, category pickers, nested settings. For a flat list use nav items; for one or two levels of sidebar sections use a shell collapsible section (nav-item--section).
tree.states: aria-expanded on a branch; aria-selected on the selected item; aria-busy while a lazy branch loads; aria-disabled
tree.markup:
• src
    • main.ts
tree.notes: Structure (WAI-ARIA tree): ul.tree[role=tree][aria-label] > li[role=none] > div.tree__item[role=treeitem] followed by a sibling ul.tree__group[role=group] holding the children in the same shape. A branch has aria-expanded ("true"/"false"); leaves do not. Every item has aria-selected. js/behaviors/tree.js (plain HTML) or react/Tree takes care of: the roving tabindex, aria-level / aria-posinset / aria-setsize, hiding the groups of collapsed branches (CSS), and the indentation. Indentation uses the custom property --tree-depth (0 for the top level), which the behaviour sets on each .tree__item; padding is --tree-depth steps of --space-4. This is the only custom property the system lets JavaScript set. Keyboard: Up/Down, Right (expand, then first child), Left (collapse, then parent), Home/End, type-ahead, Enter (select and toggle a branch), Space (select), * (expand all siblings). aria-multiselectable="true" on the tree allows several selected items (Space toggles). Events from the item (bubbling): design:select {item, selected}, design:expand {item, level, lazy}, design:collapse {item}. Lazy loading: mark a branch aria-expanded="false" with no group; on expand it gets aria-busy="true" and design:expand arrives with lazy:true; append its ul.tree__group and the busy flag clears and the items are numbered.
a11y: role=tree / treeitem / group with aria-expanded, aria-selected, and aria-level, aria-posinset, aria-setsize computed by the behaviour (the groups are siblings, so the ARIA levels carry the hierarchy).
One item is in the Tab order (roving tabindex); arrow keys move inside the tree, Tab leaves it.
Full keyboard model: Up/Down, Right/Left (expand, collapse, child, parent; swapped in right-to-left), Home/End, type-ahead by label, Enter, Space, and * to expand siblings.
The chevron is CSS-drawn and not announced; expanded/collapsed comes from aria-expanded. Selection is shown by tint plus an accent bar (an outline in forced-colours mode), not colour alone.
A lazily loading branch is aria-busy until its children arrive.
do: Give the tree an accessible name.
Keep labels short and put identifying words first (type-ahead matches the start).
Use icons to tell folders from files.
dont: Do not put interactive controls (buttons, checkboxes) inside tree items; use a table or list for that.
Do not use a tree for fewer than two levels.
Do not set --tree-depth yourself; the behaviour does.

truncate-mid.name: truncate-mid
truncate-mid.use: Middle truncation for identifiers (model names, run ids, file names, hashes, paths): the start shrinks with an ellipsis only when the box is too narrow and the last characters always stay visible, so urban_envir…_static and urban_envir…_dynamic stay different. With an optional copy button that confirms "Copied". For ordinary text that may lose its end use the layout helper truncate.
truncate-mid.states: data-tail="N" on .truncate-mid sets the characters kept at the end (default 10) when the behaviour builds the spans from plain text. The copy button is button[data-copy="value"]: it sets data-copied for 2 seconds and swaps the copy icon for a check.
truncate-mid.markup: urban_environment_model_staticurban_environment_model_static
truncate-mid.notes: Markup: span.truncate-mid (add mono for ids) > span.truncate-mid__head[aria-hidden] + span.truncate-mid__tail[aria-hidden] + span.sr-only with the full value; the full value is also the title. The wrapper takes the width it is given and never wider: a table cell of table--fixed, a list item, a kv value, a grid or flex child. In a flex or grid parent the parent must be able to shrink (min-width 0 is already set on truncate-mid and truncate-mid-row). The head has no ellipsis when everything fits. With plain HTML you can write span.truncate-mid[data-tail="10"] with only the text inside; the truncate-mid behaviour (behaviors.js) builds head, tail, sr-only text and title; markup that already has the spans is left alone. React: <TruncateMid value tail className />. Copy: wrap the value and the button in span.truncate-mid-row (a flex row: the value shrinks, the button keeps its size) and use button.btn.btn--ghost.btn--icon.btn--sm[data-copy="the full value"][aria-label="Copy model name"] with a specific label. The copy behaviour (copy.js, shared with code-block) writes the value with navigator.clipboard.writeText, falls back to execCommand and then to selecting the value; on success the icon becomes a check and a polite status says Copied (data-copied-label to translate), on failure it says Could not copy (data-failed-label) or Selected. Press Ctrl+C to copy. navigator.clipboard needs a secure context (localhost qualifies, a LAN address does not). The tail is a fixed number of characters, not as many as fit: pick a tail that contains the part that differs (the suffix of a name, the last 8 to 12 characters of an id). The copy button is a btn--icon: 24px, 44px on touch.
a11y: Head and tail are aria-hidden; one visually hidden span carries the full value, so a screen reader reads the id once and complete and find-in-page and selection still work.
The full value is also the title (hover). On touch use the copy button or the detail page.
The copy button needs a specific aria-label (Copy run id), is a keyboard-focusable 24px target (44px on touch) and announces Copied or Could not copy in a polite status.
Nothing moves: the icon swap needs no animation, so prefers-reduced-motion is respected.
do: Use mono and truncate-mid for ids, hashes, file names and paths.
Choose the tail so it holds the part that differs between values.
Show the full value on the detail page.
Give the copy button a label that names what is copied.
dont: Do not use it for sentences or labels: use truncate or let the text wrap.
Do not rely on title alone on touch screens.
Do not give the copy button a bare label such as Copy when several are on the page.

typography.name: typography
typography.use: Type roles for text that is not a plain heading or paragraph, numerals that line up, and .prose for long-form articles, documentation and marketing copy. Plain h1 to h4, p, a and code already look right without classes; reach for a role when text must look the same whatever element it sits in.
typography.markup:
Guide

Title

Introduction.

Body text with a link.
typography.states: Roles have no states. .num on a td or th also right-aligns the cell.
typography.notes: ROLES map to tokens: display = --fluid-display (2rem to 3.5rem, scales with the viewport) semibold, tight leading, tight tracking; title = font-size-3xl; heading = font-size-xl (text-heading--sm = font-size-base, used together with text-heading, for section titles above compact cards and tables); body = font-size-base (text-body--sm = font-size-sm, added after text-body, for instruction and help text); label = font-size-sm medium; caption = font-size-xs muted. Headings use text-wrap: balance, body uses text-wrap: pretty. Keep the real h1 to h4 element for the document outline and add a role only when the default size is wrong; use roles on div or span for text that must look like a title without being one. lead is the intro paragraph under a title (font-size-xl, muted). eyebrow is the small accent label above a title (uppercase, --tracking-wider). Both are plain text styles with no spacing of their own: place them in a stack. num switches Inter to tabular numerals and a slashed zero (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero, Inter features tnum and zero) so digits have equal width and columns of figures line up. Use it on table cells, prices, counters and timers. Without it Inter uses proportional digits, which is better for numbers inside running text. prose styles h1 to h4, p, ul, ol, li, blockquote, hr, figure, figcaption, img, table, th, td, pre, code, kbd, mark, abbr, dl, a and details inside it. Its column is --layout-prose-wide (44rem, roughly 70 characters per line at body size); --layout-prose (28rem) is for narrow forms and hints, not articles. Vertical rhythm comes from the space scale: space-4 between blocks, space-12 above h2, space-8 above h3, space-6 above h4. Text is not hyphenated; use ­ for a known long word. prose--wide (added to prose) removes the column limit for a document that fills the page beside a side list and holds tables. Use prose for content whose markup you do not control (rendered Markdown, CMS output, documentation). Build application screens from components, not prose. NEW TOKENS (0.5.0): --font-size-3xl (1.875rem); --fluid-display (clamp of rem and vw, used by text-display; it is its own group because the native token generators read the font-size scale as plain numbers); --tracking-{tight,normal,wide,wider} (-0.02em, 0, 0.04em, 0.08em: tight for large headings, wide for table headers, wider for eyebrows); --layout-prose-wide (44rem); --shadow-lg for large overlays, in both themes. Base element styles for blockquote, figcaption, details, kbd, mark, abbr, dl, classless tables, ::placeholder and :target were added in the base layer.
a11y: Roles are visual only: they add no heading semantics. Keep real h1 to h4 elements for the document outline, one h1 per page, and do not skip levels.
Muted text (lead, text-caption) uses --text-muted, which meets 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes; eyebrow uses the accent colour, also at least 4.5:1.
Sizes use rem and --fluid-display never goes below 2rem, so browser zoom and larger default font sizes scale it. The prose column stays at about 70 characters per line.
num changes only digit shapes, not content, so screen readers read the same text. A table of figures still needs th cells and a caption or heading.
In forced-colors mode the system palette replaces colours; blockquote, kbd, mark and code keep a visible border.
do: Use prose around rendered Markdown, documentation and marketing copy.
Use num in table cells and counters that change.
Use lead once per page, directly under the title.
dont: Do not use a role class to fake heading structure: use the right heading element.
Do not set prose on application screens; compose components instead.
Do not set font sizes in project CSS: use a role or a token.
